This appendix holds the full record for every product assessed: current facts with their claim labels and source IDs (resolve in `06_References/bibliography.xlsx`), the assessment, the classification and the scorecard (generic and regulated-FS weights). Fact cells marked *Not publicly verified* could not be confirmed from a public source and were never guessed. Disclosure: researched and drafted by an Anthropic model; Anthropic-related items were scored on the same rubric, and tiers set by the reader at checkpoints are noted in the relevant chapter.

# L9: Evaluation and observability

## MLflow (GenAI capabilities: tracing, evaluation, prompt registry, AI Gateway) (`L9-mlflow-genai`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Apache-2.0, Linux Foundation-hosted and OTel-native, with managed options on the major clouds; the most portable platform of record where an ML platform already exists [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Tracing, evaluation, monitoring, prompt registry and gateway; red-teaming not native. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | Scored on the managed route the decision tree recommends. On Amazon SageMaker and Azure ML (A1-S103), platform IAM, SSO and audit logging are presumed under rule 6 (CP2 Q1), so 4 (within the rule 2 cap of 4); platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service. The Databricks, Nebius and OpenShift AI routes are not covered by the presumption, and the open-source tracking server's own controls remain NPV. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Inherits host controls; clear Apache-2.0 licence and foundation hosting; managed-service certifications must be checked per provider. |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | Five managed services, self-host and on-premises clusters. |
| Ecosystem | 5 | OTel- and MCP-native; managed by multiple clouds; integrated by other L9 tools (Langfuse guide). |
| Reliability and maturity | 5 | Since 2018, foundation-hosted. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Free; managed pricing per provider; tracking-server operations if self-hosted. |
| Lock-in / portability | 5 | Apache-2.0, Linux Foundation governance, OTel. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **4.25 / 4.25** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rule 2 (self-hosted software) applied: NPV cap not applied; enterprise_readiness and security_compliance scored on what the software enables and on project hygiene, capped at 4; inherits host controls; Rule 6 (CP2 Q1, hyperscaler presumption) applied at CP2 rework (8 October 2026) to the SageMaker and Azure ML managed routes: enterprise_readiness 3 -> 4; platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service

**Capabilities.** Apache-2.0 AI engineering platform: OTel-based tracing of LLM applications and agents, evaluation and quality monitoring, prompt registry and optimisation, and an AI Gateway, alongside the classic ML lifecycle [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S103: MLflow README (MLflow project (Databricks-originated) (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlflow/mlflow/master/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Managed offerings on Databricks, Amazon SageMaker, Azure ML, Nebius and Red Hat OpenShift AI, plus self-hosting and on-premises clusters [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S103: MLflow README (MLflow project (Databricks-originated) (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlflow/mlflow/master/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Tracing built on OpenTelemetry; native MCP integration [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S103: MLflow README (MLflow project (Databricks-originated) (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlflow/mlflow/master/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Hosted by the Linux Foundation since 2020 under a vendor-neutral open governance model [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L9-S004: The MLflow Project Joins Linux Foundation (The Linux Foundation) <https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/press-release/the-mlflow-project-joins-linux-foundation> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Years of production use; first release June 2018 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S019: PyPI JSON metadata: mlflow (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/mlflow/json> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Limitations and risks**

- Strong Databricks association; code copyright Databricks [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S019: PyPI JSON metadata: mlflow (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/mlflow/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Security and access-control features of the open-source tracking server not verified in the fact base [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- GenAI evaluation depth relative to specialist tools not assessed in primary sources [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Spans gateway (C1) and prompt management (C5), which can blur ownership boundaries [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S103: MLflow README (MLflow project (Databricks-originated) (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlflow/mlflow/master/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Choose when**

- MLflow already holds the firm's model inventory and lifecycle on Databricks, SageMaker or Azure ML, so GenAI evidence lands beside classic model evidence [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You want the most neutral governance and licence in the layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You would self-host the open-source server without putting it behind the firm's identity and access controls [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Teams need richer agent-debugging UX than the platform offers and will not run a second tool [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L9-langfuse, L9-wandb-weave, L9-opik

**Regulated-FS note.** For firms whose model risk inventory already lives in MLflow, this is the shortest path to SS1/23-style monitoring evidence for LLM components; on SageMaker or Azure ML the platform's IAM, SSO and audit logging are presumed under CP2 Q1 but must be confirmed per service, and certifications and residency must be verified per provider [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Langfuse (`L9-langfuse`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** Acquired · **Original graphic label:** Langfuse – open source

*Rationale:* MIT core, OTel ingestion, self-hosting and certified EU Cloud make it a credible platform of record; ClickHouse ownership and the enterprise-gated audit/RBAC modules are the caveats [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Covers tracing, prompts, LLM-as-a-judge, datasets, experiments and annotation; no native red-teaming or documented trajectory metrics. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | SSO, project-level RBAC, audit logs and SCIM are documented, with SCIM, audit logs and project RBAC Enterprise-licensed when self-hosted (A1-S033): all three controls plus SCIM reach 4 under rule 7 (CP2 Q2). Not 5: SLA terms are not published and pages disagree on which tier carries SSO. |
| Security and compliance | 4 | SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA BAA and isolated EU region on Cloud; no CMK/BYOK documented, so not 5 under the layer calibration. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | SaaS, private cloud, self-host and on-prem; BYOC not verified; air-gap not documented. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | OTel-native with broad integration guides; HTTP-only OTLP. |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | GA, 555 PyPI releases since July 2023; ownership changed to ClickHouse in January 2026 with a stated unchanged roadmap. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Free MIT core and transparent Cloud pricing; ClickHouse operations and additive Enterprise pricing when self-hosted. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Base 4 (MIT core, OTel ingest, own data model) reduced by 1 for the 2026 ownership change; governance is company-controlled. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.95 / 3.85** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rule 7 (CP2 Q2) applied at CP2 rework (8 October 2026): SSO, RBAC and audit logs plus SCIM verified (A1-S033); enterprise_readiness 3 -> 4

**Capabilities.** Open-core LLM engineering platform: OTel-based tracing of LLM calls, retrieval and agent actions; prompt versioning; LLM-as-a-judge and code evaluators over ingested traces; user feedback and manual labelling; datasets, experiments and a playground; public API [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S073: Langfuse README (Langfuse / ClickHouse (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S032: OpenTelemetry (OTEL) for LLM Observability - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- MIT core covers tracing, evals, prompt management, experiments and annotation; self-hosting on Docker, Kubernetes (Helm) or Terraform templates for AWS, Azure and GCP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S023: Langfuse repository LICENSE (Langfuse / ClickHouse, Inc.) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S033: Self-Hosted Pricing - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/pricing-self-host> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S073: Langfuse README (Langfuse / ClickHouse (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Native OTLP/HTTP endpoint and OTel-based SDKs, so instrumentation is not proprietary [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S032: OpenTelemetry (OTEL) for LLM Observability - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Langfuse Cloud has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, isolated EU, US, HIPAA and Japan regions, and a DPA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S029: Security & Compliance - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S030: Data Regions & Availability - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/security/data-regions> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Published, unit-based Cloud pricing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S031: Pricing - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- Owned by ClickHouse, Inc. (announced 16 January 2026); self-hosted Enterprise tier is bundled with ClickHouse commercial offerings [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S021: ClickHouse raises $400M Series D, acquires Langfuse, launches Postgres (ClickHouse, Inc.) <https://clickhouse.com/blog/clickhouse-raises-400-million-series-d-acquires-langfuse-launches-postgres> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S033: Self-Hosted Pricing - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/pricing-self-host> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S041: ClickHouse welcomes Langfuse (with langfuse.com 'Langfuse joins ClickHouse', Orrick) <https://clickhouse.com/blog/clickhouse-acquires-langfuse-open-source-llm-observability> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- SCIM, audit logging, retention policies, project-level RBAC and server-side ingestion masking need an Enterprise licence key when self-hosted [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S033: Self-Hosted Pricing - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/pricing-self-host> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- OTLP over HTTP only (no gRPC); Langfuse-specific attributes take precedence over gen_ai.* [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S032: OpenTelemetry (OTEL) for LLM Observability - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Self-hosted telemetry is on by default (opt-out) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S033: Self-Hosted Pricing - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/pricing-self-host> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- SLA terms not published in sources reviewed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S031: Pricing - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Choose when**

- You want a self-hosted platform of record for traces, evals and prompts inside your own estate, with an MIT core and an enterprise licence for the audit and RBAC modules [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Framework-neutral instrumentation through OTel matters more than deep integration with one agent framework [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You need SCIM, audit logs and project RBAC but will not buy the Enterprise licence [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You cannot operate a ClickHouse-backed service and do not want Langfuse Cloud [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L9-langsmith, L9-opik, L9-arize-phoenix, L9-mlflow-genai

**Regulated-FS note.** Best fit for a UK/EU manager that must keep traces (which contain client data) in-region or in-estate; budget for the Enterprise licence because audit logs and project RBAC are evidence controls, not extras; disable default telemetry [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## LangSmith (`L9-langsmith`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** LangSmith – trace & eval

*Rationale:* Strongest commercial option for LangGraph estates with the certifications and deployment options FS needs. Strategic is conditional: only inside a LangGraph estate, and only with OTel dual-instrumentation as the exit route, because lock-in scores 2 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Offline and online evals, pytest plugin, prompt management and failure clustering; Engine still beta; red-teaming not native. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | SSO, RBAC, ABAC, gateway audit logging and support SLA on Enterprise; SCIM not documented in the fact base. |
| Security and compliance | 4 | SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, HIPAA BAA, EU region; no CMK/BYOK documented, so not 5 under the layer calibration. |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | SaaS (US/EU), BYOC (AWS), self-hosted and air-gapped self-host on Enterprise. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | Large LangChain ecosystem plus OTLP ingest; native format preferred. |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | GA since 2023, 536 SDK releases, independent and funded (US$125M Series B, October 2025). |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | Transparent but per-seat plus per-trace; heavy self-host footprint. |
| Lock-in / portability | 2 | Proprietary platform, native format recommended, growing bundling with the agent runtime. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.95 / 3.80** | |

**Capabilities.** Proprietary observability, evaluation and deployment platform: native and OTel trace ingest, offline and online evaluation on datasets, prompt management, pytest plugin, and hosted agent deployment; now also Engine (beta), Fleet, Sandboxes and an LLM Gateway [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S034: Set up LangSmith (deployment options) - Docs by LangChain (LangChain, Inc.) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/platform-setup> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S037: Introducing End-to-End OpenTelemetry Support in LangSmith (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/blog/end-to-end-opentelemetry-langsmith> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S039: Everything we shipped at Interrupt (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/blog/interrupt-2026-overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S108: LangSmith Python SDK README (LangChain, Inc. (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/langsmith-sdk/main/python/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Deepest coupling to LangGraph/LangChain, the orchestration framework many teams already use [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S037: Introducing End-to-End OpenTelemetry Support in LangSmith (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/blog/end-to-end-opentelemetry-langsmith> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S039: Everything we shipped at Interrupt (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/blog/interrupt-2026-overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, HIPAA (BAA on Enterprise) and GDPR; US or EU managed regions on all tiers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S036: LangSmith Regions FAQ - Docs by LangChain (LangChain, Inc.) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/regions-faq> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S126: LangSmith Engine security - Docs by LangChain (LangChain, Inc.) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- SaaS, BYOC on AWS, self-hosted and air-gapped self-host on Enterprise [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S034: Set up LangSmith (deployment options) - Docs by LangChain (LangChain, Inc.) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/platform-setup> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Enterprise SSO, RBAC and ABAC; support SLA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S035: LangSmith Plans and Pricing (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- Native tracing format is recommended over OTel for performance, which pulls instrumentation towards a proprietary format [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S037: Introducing End-to-End OpenTelemetry Support in LangSmith (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/blog/end-to-end-opentelemetry-langsmith> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Platform increasingly bundles the LangChain agent runtime (Fleet, Deployment), widening the blast radius of a vendor change [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S039: Everything we shipped at Interrupt (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/blog/interrupt-2026-overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Self-hosting needs at least 16 vCPU / 64 GB plus PostgreSQL, Redis and ClickHouse [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S034: Set up LangSmith (deployment options) - Docs by LangChain (LangChain, Inc.) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/platform-setup> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Per-seat Plus pricing plus per-trace overage [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S035: LangSmith Plans and Pricing (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- LangSmith Engine is public beta [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S039: Everything we shipped at Interrupt (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/blog/interrupt-2026-overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Choose when**

- LangGraph is your orchestration standard and you want one supported platform for traces, evals and deployment [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You need a commercial vendor with SOC 2, ISO 27001 and an EU region, or BYOC/self-host for residency [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- Your agents are framework-heterogeneous and you want a neutral trace store [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You do not want the observability vendor to also be your agent runtime vendor [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L9-langfuse, L9-braintrust, L9-arize-ax

**Regulated-FS note.** Use the EU region or self-host for client data; instrument with OTel GenAI conventions even if native SDKs are also used, so the evidence trail survives a platform exit; keep Engine-proposed fixes behind change control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Ecosystem | 4 | Many framework integrations; OTel export mainly to Confident AI. |

## Promptfoo (`L9-promptfoo`)

**Tier:** Tactical · **Flags:** Acquired · **Original graphic label:** Promptfoo – red-teaming

*Rationale:* Valuable eval and red-team harness under MIT, but now owned by a model vendor with an unpublished closing date; use as one of two red-team tools, not the sole independent check [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Regression evals, red-teaming, model comparison and PR code scanning; not a production trace store. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Enterprise RBAC, team management, SLA and professional services; SSO and audit logs not documented. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Scored as a locally run MIT CLI (rule 2): inherits host controls, local-only execution. Enterprise SaaS certifications are NPV and would cap that edition at 2. |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | Local CLI, Enterprise SaaS, and On-Prem on AWS, Azure or GCP with a dedicated runner. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | CI integrations, OTLP receiver, many providers, OWASP/NIST reports. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Frequent releases since 2023 but pre-1.0; acquisition announced 9 March 2026, closing not published. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Free MIT CLI; attack-generation and grader model spend. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Base 4 (MIT, portable configs) reduced by 1 for the announced acquisition; governance is vendor-controlled. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.70 / 3.55** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rule 2 (self-hosted software) applied: NPV cap not applied; enterprise_readiness and security_compliance scored on what the software enables and on project hygiene, capped at 4; inherits host controls

**Capabilities.** MIT CLI and library for automated evaluation of prompts, models and agents, red-teaming and vulnerability scanning, side-by-side model comparison, CI/CD checks and pull-request code scanning for LLM security issues; Promptfoo Enterprise as SaaS or On-Prem [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S062: Promptfoo README (Promptfoo (OpenAI) (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S063: Promptfoo Enterprise docs (SaaS and On-Prem) (Promptfoo (OpenAI) (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/main/site/docs/enterprise/index.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

## Arize Phoenix (`L9-arize-phoenix`)

**Tier:** Tactical · **Flags:** Acquired · **Original graphic label:** Phoenix – Atrace

*Rationale:* Useful, portable workbench with strong instrumentation; ELv2, no audit trail, community-only support and new Dynatrace ownership make it unsuitable as the production record [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Tracing, retrieval and response evals, datasets, experiments, prompt management and pytest; online production monitoring is the AX proposition. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Scored as self-hosted software (rule 2). With authentication enabled, Phoenix provides admin, member and viewer roles and login through OAuth2 identity providers (A1-S105): two of SSO, RBAC and audit logs verified, so 3 under rule 7 (CP2 Q2). No audit trail, SCIM or commercial support for Phoenix itself, so not above 3. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Inherits host controls; licence is clear, telemetry can be disabled; auth off by default is a hygiene weakness. Certifications NPV for Phoenix Cloud, not used. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Self-host, private-cloud templates and air-gap; Phoenix Cloud low confidence; no BYOC. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | OpenInference is accepted by other backends; broad framework and provider auto-instrumentation. |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | 700 releases since January 2023; Dynatrace completed acquisition 1 October 2026 with a support commitment. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Free with no caps; one instance per team and PostgreSQL to operate. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Base 4 (portable OTel/OpenInference, source-available) reduced by 1 for the 2026 ownership change; ELv2 is not permissive. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.65 / 3.50** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rule 2 (self-hosted software) applied: NPV cap not applied; enterprise_readiness and security_compliance scored on what the software enables and on project hygiene, capped at 4; inherits host controls; Rule 7 (CP2 Q2) applied at CP2 rework (8 October 2026) for consistency with Opik and Unstructured: roles and OAuth2 IdP login verified (A1-S105); enterprise_readiness 2 -> 3; no audit trail

**Capabilities.** Self-hosted tracing and evaluation built on OpenTelemetry and OpenInference: LLM-based response and retrieval evaluations, versioned datasets, experiments, prompt playground and management, REST API, MCP endpoint and a pytest plugin for eval-in-CI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S066: Arize Phoenix README (Arize AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S049: OpenInference LICENSE (Apache-2.0) (Arize AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Arize-ai/openinference/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S106: Phoenix: Eval CI with pytest (docs source) (Arize AI (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/main/docs/phoenix/datasets-and-experiments/how-to-experiments/eval-ci-with-pytest.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].

# L8: Data extraction, ingestion and web

## Docling (`L8-docling`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** Docling – doc parser

*Rationale:* MIT, foundation-governed and self-hostable, so it can anchor the firm's canonical document model; enterprise controls are built around it.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Broad formats, OCR, VLM and chunking; no ACL, PII or lineage, and table accuracy not independently verified. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Library rule: inherits host controls; docling-serve gives an API boundary; commercial managed option via IBM watsonx. |
| Security and compliance | 4 | Library rule: MIT; SECURITY.md with private vulnerability reporting, OpenSSF Best Practices badge participation and cryptographically signed releases on PyPI, Quay.io and GHCR [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S001: Security and Disclosure Information Policy for the Docling Project (Docling Project (LF AI & Data)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/.github/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08]; IBM offers a managed service. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Self-hosted, private cloud, on-prem and an IBM-managed service; air-gap not explicitly documented. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | MCP server, REST server and agent-framework integrations; LF AI & Data project. |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | Graduate-tier foundation project with steady releases; rapid minor-version churn. |
| Cost / TCO | 5 | Free; CPU sufficient for standard pipelines, GPU only for VLM/ASR paths [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. |
| Lock-in / portability | 5 | MIT, open format, neutral governance. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **4.00 / 4.05** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Library rule applied (enterprise_readiness and security_compliance scored on what the library enables and project hygiene; inherits host controls)

**Capabilities.** Open-source conversion of PDF, Office, legacy Office, HTML, images, audio and video into a unified DoclingDocument, with OCR, VLM pipelines, ASR and hybrid chunking; runs as a library, CLI, docling-serve REST API or MCP server [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S057: Docling README (Docling Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S111: Docling supported formats (docs source) (Docling Project (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/docs/usage/supported_formats.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S082: Docling Serve README (Docling Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling-serve/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- MIT licence and LF AI & Data governance (donated March 2025; Graduate tier August 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S057: Docling README (Docling Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S091: Docling - LF AI & Data project page; LF press release 29 April 2025 (IBM contributes Docling, Data Prep Kit, BeeAI) (LF AI & Data Foundation) <https://lfaidata.foundation/projects/docling/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Local or self-hosted processing keeps documents in the firm's estate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Broad format coverage including PPTX, XLSX and legacy Office [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S111: Docling supported formats (docs source) (Docling Project (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/docs/usage/supported_formats.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- A documented canonical representation (DoclingDocument) that can serve as the firm's internal document model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Limitations and risks**

- No ACL, PII or lineage features in the README or docs navigation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S057: Docling README (Docling Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Very fast release cadence (2.135.0 on 7 October 2026; 223 releases in about two years) makes version pinning mandatory [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S008: PyPI JSON metadata: docling (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/docling/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Individual models carry their own licences, which need separate review [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S057: Docling README (Docling Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- A security policy with private vulnerability reporting, OpenSSF Best Practices badge participation and signed releases is published [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S001: Security and Disclosure Information Policy for the Docling Project (Docling Project (LF AI & Data)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/.github/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08]

**Choose when**

- Documents must not leave the firm's estate
- You want an open canonical document model that survives a change of parser or OCR engine

**Avoid when**

- You need managed, permission-aware connectors out of the box
- You have no platform team to run, pin and patch a Python service

**Nearest competitors:** L8-unstructured, L8-mineru, L8-llamaparse

**Regulated-FS note.** Default self-hosted parser for client and confidential documents; pin the docling version and each model version in a parse manifest so that a parse can be reproduced for audit [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Unstructured: open-source 'unstructured' library and 'unstructured-ingest' connectors; commercial Transform v2 API / platform (`L8-unstructured`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** Renamed · **Original graphic label:** Unstructured – ETL for docs

*Rationale:* The open-source ingest connectors are the only verified source of ACL metadata and incremental reprocessing in L8, with an in-VPC commercial path.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Partitioning, chunking and the only verified ACL-aware incremental connectors; best table quality is API-only. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | SAML 2.0/OIDC SSO and account- and workspace-level roles mapped from IdP groups on Business deployments [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S016: Unstructured: IdP overview, Configure an identity provider, Security and compliance overview (Unstructured Technologies) <https://docs.unstructured.io/business/idp/overview> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; no workspace audit log documented (stdout logging for the customer's own collection), so 3. |
| Security and compliance | 4 | Vendor-listed SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA and CMMC 2.0 Level 2 (medium confidence); FedRAMP wording is 'alignment' only and is not relied on; data region not verified. |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | Shared SaaS, dedicated, in-VPC, self-hosted open source and vendor-marketed on-prem/air-gapped. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | Large connector catalogue into vector stores and warehouses. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Four years of releases, but pre-1.0 library and a PyPI/changelog version mismatch. |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | Open source free; API pricing published but conflicting. |
| Lock-in / portability | 4 | Apache-2.0 library and connectors; proprietary API for best models. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.80 / 3.85** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* NPV cap lifted at CP2 review (8 October 2026): SSO and RBAC verified (B-REV-S016); audit-log feature not documented; Rule 7 (CP2 Q2) checked at CP2 rework: SSO and RBAC verified, audit logs not documented, so 3 kept (maximum without all three controls)

**Capabilities.** Apache-2.0 'unstructured' partitioning library and 'unstructured-ingest' connectors (SharePoint including Teams channel files, OneDrive, Confluence, Salesforce, S3 and others) that move data to vector stores and warehouses; commercial Transform v2 API with shared, dedicated and in-VPC tiers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S075: Unstructured open-source library README (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S094: unstructured-ingest CHANGELOG (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured-ingest/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S117: Unstructured Pricing Plans for Data Processing <https://unstructured.io/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S019: Unstructured Transform: Parse your first document (API v2) <https://docs.unstructured.io/transform/first-request> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- Only L8 product with verified permission-aware ingestion: a permissions_version SHA-256 ACL digest that triggers reprocessing on ACL-only change [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S094: unstructured-ingest CHANGELOG (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured-ingest/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Distinguishes an unavailable permission fetch from an empty permission set [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S094: unstructured-ingest CHANGELOG (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured-ingest/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Vendor lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA and CMMC 2.0 Level 2 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S117: Unstructured Pricing Plans for Data Processing <https://unstructured.io/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S090: Unstructured API overview (compliance list); pricing; CMMC 2.0 Level 2 blog <https://docs.unstructured.io/api-reference/overview> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Open-source library and connectors stay free, so the pipeline can run in the firm's estate [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S075: Unstructured open-source library README (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Limitations and risks**

- No workspace audit-log feature is documented; logs go to stdout for the customer's own collection [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S016: Unstructured: IdP overview, Configure an identity provider, Security and compliance overview (Unstructured Technologies) <https://docs.unstructured.io/business/idp/overview> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Highest-quality models only via the proprietary API [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S075: Unstructured open-source library README (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Library still pre-1.0 after four years (0.27.16) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S011: PyPI JSON metadata: unstructured (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/unstructured/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Per-page price conflict (US$0.015 vs US$0.03) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S117: Unstructured Pricing Plans for Data Processing <https://unstructured.io/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S118: Unstructured Transform billing <https://docs.unstructured.io/transform/billing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Library sends usage analytics by default [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S075: Unstructured open-source library README (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Choose when**

- You need connector-level ACL capture and incremental reprocessing from SharePoint, OneDrive or Confluence
- You want one pipeline that can run as open source in-estate or as an in-VPC commercial tier

**Avoid when**

- You need a documented, exportable audit log on the hosted service today
- Your corpus is mostly scanned or table-heavy and you will not pay for the API models [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L8-docling, L8-llamaparse, L8-reducto

**Regulated-FS note.** The connector ACL digest is the nearest thing in this layer to entitlement-preserving ingestion; disable default analytics and confirm the hosted data region before any client data is sent [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Tier:** Tactical · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** Mistral OCR – OCR

*Rationale:* A good EU or self-managed OCR engine to sit behind an interface, but short model-retirement windows make it a component, not a foundation.

Not 5: audit-log export is not supported, OIDC is not supported and SLA terms are NPV. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Company-level SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and ISO 27701; OCR scope unconfirmed. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | EU SaaS, private cloud, self-managed container and on-prem under enterprise agreement. |
| Ecosystem | 3 | Mistral SDKs with opt-in OTel spans; usable inside other parsers. |
| Reliability and maturity | 2 | OCR 4.0 retired about five weeks after 4.1 reached GA; frequent version replacement. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | US$4 per 1,000 pages, US$2 batch; self-host pricing unpublished. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Proprietary model, but text/JSON output is easy to swap behind an interface. |

**Capabilities.** Mistral OCR 4.1 (alias mistral-ocr-latest), part of Mistral Document AI: OCR endpoint returning structured output with bounding boxes, block labels, table formatting, header/footer extraction and block-level confidence scores [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S083: Mistral Python SDK: OCR operation docs (Mistral AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mistralai/client-python/main/docs/sdks/ocr/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S130: OCR 4.1 - Mistral AI docs <https://docs.mistral.ai/models/ocr-4-1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

- Self-managed single-container, private-cloud and on-prem deployment for enterprise customers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S135: Mistral OCR 4 : SOTA OCR for Document Intelligence (Mistral AI) <https://mistral.ai/news/ocr-4/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Low published price: US$4 per 1,000 pages, US$2 in batch [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S130: OCR 4.1 - Mistral AI docs <https://docs.mistral.ai/models/ocr-4-1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S010: OCR 4.1 model card / changelog / pricing (Mistral AI) <https://docs.mistral.ai/models/ocr-4-1> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- Model-version churn: OCR 4.1 GA 26 August 2026 and OCR 4.0 retired 30 September 2026; the original model is no longer maintained [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S130: OCR 4.1 - Mistral AI docs <https://docs.mistral.ai/models/ocr-4-1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S014: Mistral docs Changelog; OCR 4.0 model page; OCR 4 governance page (Mistral AI) <https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/changelogs> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]

- Self-hosting licence terms and hardware sizing not published [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- OCR only: no connectors, ACL, PII or lineage [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Audit logs cannot be exported [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S015: Mistral docs: Audit logs (Mistral AI) <https://docs.mistral.ai/admin/security-access/audit-logs> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], so the firm cannot hold them in its own archive without a vendor export route [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- You need an EU-resident or self-managed OCR engine behind your own parsing pipeline
- Scanned documents dominate and cost per page matters

**Avoid when**

- You cannot re-validate within a deprecation window of weeks
- You call the 'latest' alias in production

**Nearest competitors:** L8-google-document-ai, L8-docling, L8-reducto

**Regulated-FS note.** Pin the dated model ID (not mistral-ocr-latest), store OCR outputs with the model ID, and treat each model retirement as a change-control event with re-validation [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Library, Docker server, private cloud, on-prem and hosted cloud. |
| Ecosystem | 3 | MCP for common coding assistants; smaller ecosystem than commercial peers. |

**Capabilities.** Open-source crawler and scraper producing LLM-ready Markdown or structured data with browser automation, batch crawling and LLM extraction; Python library, CLI, self-hosted REST server, MCP and a hosted Crawl4AI Cloud [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S074: Crawl4AI README (UncleCode / Crawl4AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unclecode/crawl4ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

- Pre-1.0 (0.9.4) with a single-maintainer origin [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S009: PyPI JSON metadata: crawl4ai (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/crawl4ai/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S074: Crawl4AI README (UncleCode / Crawl4AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unclecode/crawl4ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]

- No certifications or enterprise support found [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- Self-hosted crawling of a small set of approved public sources by a team that can own it
- Prototyping web acquisition before committing to a commercial service

**Avoid when**

- It would be a critical production dependency without a support route
- Legal cannot accept the attribution clause for your use

**Nearest competitors:** L8-firecrawl, L8-apify

**Regulated-FS note.** Acceptable for public data in a controlled estate; record the attribution clause in the open-source register and do not use the hosted cloud for anything confidential [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Sentence Transformers (sentence-transformers library; SBERT.net) (`L7-sentence-transformers`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** SBERT – Sentence transformers

*Rationale:* The portable, self-hosted toolkit for embeddings, reranking, sparse and late interaction; the firm's exit route and fine-tuning base.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |

| Technical | 4 | Covers dense, cross-encoder, sparse and multi-vector with fine-tuning; quality depends on the chosen model. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Rule 2: enables in-estate serving and fine-tuning; no commercial support verified (capped at 4). |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Rule 2: Apache-2.0; SECURITY.md with private vulnerability reporting and CVE issuance through GitHub advisories (B-REV-S002); release signing not verified; inherits host controls. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Self-host, on-prem and air-gap; no managed option of its own. |
| Ecosystem | 5 | Over 15,000 models on Hugging Face; many MTEB models load through it. |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | Since 2019, regular 2026 releases, Hugging Face stewardship. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Free; compute and operations are the cost. |
| Lock-in / portability | 4 | Apache-2.0 and model-agnostic; stewarded by one company rather than a neutral foundation. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.80 / 3.70** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rule 2 (self-hosted library): enterprise_readiness and security_compliance capped at 4; NPV cap not applied

**Capabilities.** Apache-2.0 Python library (6.1.0, 18 September 2026) for dense embeddings, Cross-Encoder rerankers, Sparse Encoders and Multi-Vector Encoders (ColBERT-style late interaction), with training and fine-tuning; over 15,000 pre-trained models on Hugging Face [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S029: sentence-transformers - PyPI (PyPI / Hugging Face (maintainer)) <https://pypi.org/project/sentence-transformers/> accessed 2026-10-07; A2-S032: sentence-transformers PyPI JSON API <https://pypi.org/pypi/sentence-transformers/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A2-S028: Sentence Transformers is joining Hugging Face! <https://huggingface.co/blog/sentence-transformers-joins-hf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Maintained by Hugging Face [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S028: Sentence Transformers is joining Hugging Face! <https://huggingface.co/blog/sentence-transformers-joins-hf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S092: Sentence Transformers is joining Hugging Face! <https://huggingface.co/blog/sentence-transformers-joins-hf> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- One toolkit for the whole retrieval-optimisation layer: bi-encoder, cross-encoder, sparse and late interaction [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S029: sentence-transformers - PyPI (PyPI / Hugging Face (maintainer)) <https://pypi.org/project/sentence-transformers/> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Fine-tuning on in-domain pairs is the main route to domain adaptation without a vendor [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S029: sentence-transformers - PyPI (PyPI / Hugging Face (maintainer)) <https://pypi.org/project/sentence-transformers/> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Model-agnostic and permissively licensed, so it is the natural exit route from any hosted embedding API [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Limitations and risks**

- A library, not a model: quality depends on the model chosen and on the firm's evaluation [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- No commercial support offer verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}; a security policy with private reporting and CVE issuance exists [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S002: sentence-transformers Security Policy (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/main/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08], but release signing is not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Depends on Hugging Face stewardship and a small maintainer team [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Model licences on the Hub vary; each model needs its own licence check (for example, Jina weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S024: Legal Information - Jina AI (Jina AI (Elastic)) <https://jina.ai/legal/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- Embeddings or reranking must run inside the firm's estate, including air-gapped
- Domain fine-tuning or a reproducible, pinned retrieval stack is required

**Avoid when**

- There is no team to operate model serving, patching and evaluation
- A vendor SLA is mandatory for the retrieval path

**Nearest competitors:** L7-nvidia-nemo-retriever, L7-qwen3-embedding, L7-cohere

**Regulated-FS note.** Inherits host controls: residency, access and logging are whatever the firm's platform provides [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Pin library and model versions and record both in the evidence pack [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

Form 10-K FY2026 (Voyage AI acquisition note) and IR release 24 Feb 2025 (MongoDB, Inc. (SEC EDGAR)) <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1441816/000162828026016799/mdb-20260131.htm> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; roadmap now tied to MongoDB [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Certifications rest on a homepage listing; trust-portal report scope not verified [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A2-S044: MongoDB Voyage AI Models in AWS (Marketplace model package) (Voyage AI (MongoDB)) <https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/aws-marketplace-model-package> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; MongoDB points standalone Voyage to a separate trust portal [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S138: MongoDB Atlas Trust Center <https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform/trust> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- rerank-3 is Preview on MongoDB's lifecycle page; Atlas Embedding and Reranking API and Automated Embedding are public preview [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S024: rerank-3 and rerank-3-lite: the next generation of Voyage rerankers; MongoDB Voyage model lifecycle page (Voyage AI by MongoDB) <https://blog.voyageai.com/2026/09/30/rerank-3/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A2-S077: Introducing the Embedding and Reranking API on MongoDB Atlas <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-the-embedding-and-reranking-api-on-mongodb-atlas> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S078: Unlocking AI Search: Introducing Automated Embedding in MongoDB Vector Search <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/unlocking-ai-search-introducing-automated-embedding-in-mongodb-vector-search> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Only voyage-4-nano can be self-hosted [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S071: Embeddings - Claude Platform Docs (Anthropic) <https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/embeddings> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Vendor claims that rerank-3 beats competitors are not decision inputs [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A2-S141: Context Engineering Has a Retrieval Issue: Introducing rerank-3 and Native Reranking (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-rerank-3-and-native-rerank> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Atlas roles govern who can create, edit or delete model API keys [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S028: Manage Voyage AI Model API Keys (and Organization and Project Access) (MongoDB, Inc.) <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/voyageai/management/api-keys/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], but SSO and audit logging of key use are not stated [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- MongoDB is the L6 store, or the firm accepts MongoDB as a strategic supplier
- Finance-domain vocabulary and contextualised chunks matter, subject to in-domain evaluation
- EU processing via the Atlas Europe Geography is acceptable

**Avoid when**

- UK processing or on-premises hosting of the main models is mandatory
- Independence between the retrieval-store vendor and the embedding vendor is a concentration requirement

**Nearest competitors:** L7-cohere, L7-jina, L7-qwen3-embedding, L7-openai

**Regulated-FS note.** The Atlas Embedding and Reranking API offers an EEA Geography with no fallback outside it, at a 10% premium [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S142: Europe Data Residency for Atlas Embedding and Reranking (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/europe-data-residency-for-atlas-embedding-reranking> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Automated Embedding and Native Reranking do not yet support Geography targeting [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S142: Europe Data Residency for Atlas Embedding and Reranking (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/europe-data-residency-for-atlas-embedding-reranking> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Request the Voyage SOC 2 report and its scope before use with client data [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## NVIDIA NeMo Retriever embedding and reranking NIM microservices (Nemotron embedding/reranking models) (`L7-nvidia-nemo-retriever`)

**Tier:** Tactical · **Flags:** Renamed · **Original graphic label:** NVIDIA – Embed

*Rationale:* Sound self-hosted runtime for NVIDIA-standardised estates; licence cost and GPU coupling make it a poor neutral default.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 3 | Embed and rerank including multimodal; shorter context and fixed dimensions; Matryoshka not evidenced. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Commercial subscription with Helm/Kubernetes deployment; inherits host IAM; support terms NPV. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Self-hosted container (certifications not applicable); licence clear; container hardening evidence NPV. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Any cloud or data centre with supported GPUs, NVIDIA API Catalog for development; air-gap NPV. |
| Ecosystem | 3 | NeMo Retriever pipeline and Helm chart; wider ecosystem NPV. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Frequent NIM releases; inconsistent version dating across pages. |
| Cost / TCO | 2 | Per-GPU licence on top of GPU infrastructure. |
| Lock-in / portability | 2 | Tied to NVIDIA GPUs and the AI Enterprise licence; per-model licences vary. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.00 / 2.95** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* NPV cap not applied to security_compliance: self-hosted container, vendor certifications not applicable; scored on in-estate deployment and licence clarity; Rule 6 (CP2 Q1) not applied at CP2 rework: no hyperscaler-consumed route is in the fact base; scores kept

**Capabilities.** NVIDIA NeMo Retriever embedding and reranking NIM microservices: Embedding NIM 2.3 (nemotron-3-embed-1b added in 2.2; llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2; llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2) and Reranking NIM 2.0.0 (llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2, rerank-1b-v2, rerank-500m-v2), deployed by Helm on Kubernetes or Docker [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S030: Release Notes for NVIDIA NeMo Retriever Reranking NIM <https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/nemo-retriever/text-reranking/latest/release-notes.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S031: Get Started With NVIDIA NeMo Retriever Embedding NIM (2.3) <https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/nemo-retriever/embedding/2.3/getting-started.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S094: NeMo Retriever Embedding NIM release notes / overview / support matrix (NVIDIA) <https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/nemo-retriever/embedding/2.2/release-notes.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- Embed and rerank, text and multimodal, as GPU-optimised containers that run in any cloud or data centre with supported GPUs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S031: Get Started With NVIDIA NeMo Retriever Embedding NIM (2.3) <https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/nemo-retriever/embedding/2.3/getting-started.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S040: General NIM FAQ (NVIDIA) <https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/docs/product> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Client data stays in the firm's environment when self-hosted [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Fits estates that already standardise on NVIDIA AI Enterprise for L2 serving [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Limitations and risks**

- Production use requires NVIDIA AI Enterprise, from US$4,500 per GPU per year or about US$1 per GPU per hour in cloud (as of 7 October 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S040: General NIM FAQ (NVIDIA) <https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/docs/product> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Two-layer licensing (container agreement plus per-model licences that vary) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S041: Governing Terms for NVIDIA NeMo Retriever Embedding NIM <https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/nemo-retriever/embedding/2.3/eula.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Shorter limits than API peers: nemotron-3-embed-1b is text-only, fixed 2,048 dims, 4,096-token maximum [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S094: NeMo Retriever Embedding NIM release notes / overview / support matrix (NVIDIA) <https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/nemo-retriever/embedding/2.2/release-notes.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A2-S031: Get Started With NVIDIA NeMo Retriever Embedding NIM (2.3) <https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/nemo-retriever/embedding/2.3/getting-started.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Helm chart warns that a text-only reranker silently degrades multimodal reranking [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S031: Get Started With NVIDIA NeMo Retriever Embedding NIM (2.3) <https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/nemo-retriever/embedding/2.3/getting-started.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Release dates inconsistent across NGC and Hugging Face pages; container security features NPV

**Choose when**

- The firm already licenses NVIDIA AI Enterprise and runs GPU Kubernetes
- A vendor-supported, self-hosted embed-plus-rerank runtime is required

**Avoid when**

- Retrieval volumes do not justify per-GPU licences
- The firm wants to avoid deepening GPU-vendor concentration

**Nearest competitors:** L7-sentence-transformers, L7-qwen3-embedding, L7-cohere

**Regulated-FS note.** Self-hosting removes cross-border transfer questions for the retrieval path [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}; the AI Enterprise subscription becomes the third-party arrangement to register [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

# L6: Retrieval and knowledge stores

## Elasticsearch (Elastic Search AI Platform) (`L6-elasticsearch`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** Elasticsearch – hybrid search

*Rationale:* Strategic, conditional: where Elastic is already operated, because cost scores 2 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 5 | BM25, quantised vectors, RRF/linear fusion, restrictive-filter optimisation and document-level security cover the layer's research questions |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | SAML/OIDC SSO, RBAC, DLS/FLS and audit logging (A2-S134; Elastic Cloud SSO/RBAC B-REV-S019), plus the Elastic Cloud API with role-bearing organisation API keys (B-REVA-S003): rule 7 allows 4; SCIM not found, Cloud audit tier and SLA not confirmed |
| Security and compliance | 5 | Elastic Cloud ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II within the product, plus CMK |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Hosted and Serverless on three clouds, self-managed and on-prem; no BYOC evidenced |
| Ecosystem | 5 | De-facto search standard; REST; OpenSearch fork |
| Reliability and maturity | 5 | Years of production use; frequent minors |
| Cost / TCO | 2 | Paid tiers for key security features; cluster pricing not verified; operations heavy |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | AGPL option but paid features proprietary; SSPL/ELv2 alternatives (rule 4) |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **4.30 / 4.25** | |

**Capabilities.** Distributed search engine combining BM25, dense/sparse vectors (BBQ/DiskBBQ default since 9.1), RRF and linear hybrid retrievers, semantic_text auto-embedding (Jina v5 default) and document-level security; Elastic 9.5 GA 4 August 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S134: Use a customer-managed encryption key - Elastic Cloud <https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/security/encrypt-deployment-with-customer-managed-encryption-key> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S085: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration; Elastic community newsletter August 2026 <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- Mature lexical plus vector and hybrid retrieval in one engine [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Field- and document-level security maps to entitlement-aware retrieval [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S134: Use a customer-managed encryption key - Elastic Cloud <https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/security/encrypt-deployment-with-customer-managed-encryption-key> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Elastic Cloud ISO 27001/27017/27018, SOC 2 Type II; CMK on Hosted Enterprise; Private Link incl. London [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S045: Elastic Trust Center <https://www.elastic.co/trust> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S134: Use a customer-managed encryption key - Elastic Cloud <https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/security/encrypt-deployment-with-customer-managed-encryption-key> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

## PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension (`L6-pgvector`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** Postgres – + pgvector

*Rationale:* Lowest-increment, permissively licensed, transactionally integrated option on every hyperscaler; the default answer to 'do we need a dedicated vector DB?' [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Dense+sparse, HNSW/IVFFlat, filter-aware scans and SQL joins; no native BM25 and scale limits keep it below 5 |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | Rule 2: inherits host controls; consumed via RDS/Aurora, Azure or Cloud SQL/AlloyDB so platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Rule 2 hygiene: permissive licence and prompt CVE fixes, but two 2026 memory-safety CVEs (one CVSS 8.8) and host patch lag; signed releases not verified |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | Self-host, on-prem and air-gap, plus managed services on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud |
| Ecosystem | 5 | SQL; supported by all three hyperscalers' managed PostgreSQL and Bedrock Knowledge Bases via Aurora |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | Active 0.8.x maintenance (five 2026 releases) on a long-established database; still pre-1.0 versioning |
| Cost / TCO | 5 | Free; cost is PostgreSQL compute and RAM already operated |
| Lock-in / portability | 5 | PostgreSQL License, SQL interface, multiple managed hosts |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **4.25 / 4.20** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rule 2 (self-hosted software): security scored on project hygiene; enterprise readiness on host controls with CP2 Q1 presumption for managed hyperscaler PostgreSQL

**Capabilities.** PostgreSQL extension adding vector types (incl. sparsevec) and HNSW/IVFFlat ANN indexes, so vectors sit beside relational data and SQL filters; iterative index scans and filter-aware index selection since 0.8.0; 0.8.7 released 1 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S063: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector project) <https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S061: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group (news post by pgvector p) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S020: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-08; V1-S022: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- Transactional integration: vectors, metadata and entitlement tables in one ACID database [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- PostgreSQL License (permissive, OSI) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S021: pgvector LICENSE (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-08]
- Managed on Amazon RDS/Aurora, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Cloud SQL and AlloyDB [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S004: Extension versions for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL; RDS PostgreSQL release notes; Aurora pgvector announcements (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/PostgreSQLReleaseNotes/postgresql-extensions.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L6-S005: Vector search in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server; Cloud SQL vector embeddings; AlloyDB vector search overview (Microsoft; Google Cloud) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/extensions/how-to-use-pgvector> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Security fixes shipped promptly in 2026 (0.8.2, 0.8.7) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S020: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-08; V1-S022: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- CVE-2026-103484 (CVSS 8.8, IVFFlat build, possible code execution) fixed in 0.8.7; CVE-2026-3172 fixed in 0.8.2 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S022: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A2-S062: pgvector 0.8.2 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group (news post by pgvector p) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-082-released-3245/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Managed hosts lag upstream (latest RDS release seen carries 0.8.2) and Azure manages the version [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S004: Extension versions for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL; RDS PostgreSQL release notes; Aurora pgvector announcements (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/PostgreSQLReleaseNotes/postgresql-extensions.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L6-S005: Vector search in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server; Cloud SQL vector embeddings; AlloyDB vector search overview (Microsoft; Google Cloud) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/extensions/how-to-use-pgvector> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- No BM25 ranking in the extension; hybrid needs sparsevec or app-side fusion [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S063: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector project) <https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- HNSW indexes are memory-hungry; large-scale filtered behaviour not evidenced [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- PostgreSQL is a firm standard and the corpus is millions, not billions, of chunks [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Entitlements already live in relational tables [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- Thousands of isolated tenants with independent scaling are needed [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Low-latency search over a very large corpus under selective filters [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L6-mongodb-atlas-vector-search, L6-elasticsearch, L6-qdrant

**Regulated-FS note.** Default for UK/EU managed PostgreSQL; track host pgvector version against CVEs; restrict index-creation rights; one schema per segregated mandate [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Qdrant (open-source vector search engine; Qdrant Cloud, Hybrid Cloud, Private Cloud) (`L6-qdrant`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** Qdrant – open source

*Rationale:* Permissive licence, filter-aware multi-tenant engine and air-gap-capable deployment make it the default dedicated engine when a trigger is met [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Dense/sparse, ACORN filtering, RRF, multitenancy, quantisation; BM25 not evidenced |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | Cloud RBAC with custom roles, SSO (Premium add-on) and audit access logging (B-L6-S007), plus the Cloud Management API and a 99.9% (99.95% multi-AZ) SLA on Premium (B-REVA-S002): rule 7 allows 4; SCIM not verified |
| Security and compliance | 3 | SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA but no ISO 27001: maximum 3 in this layer |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | SaaS, hybrid, private incl. air-gap, self-host |
| Ecosystem | 4 | REST/gRPC with OpenAPI, FastEmbed, three clouds |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Frequent releases but breaking storage migration at 1.16; vendor-governed |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Free OSS; managed from US$25 (as captured) |

## MongoDB Vector Search (Atlas; self-managed Community Edition and Enterprise Advanced) (`L6-mongodb-atlas-vector-search`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** MongoDB – Atlas vector

*Rationale:* Strategic, conditional: only where MongoDB is already the operational store, because lock-in scores 2; the condition is an existing platform commitment, which is why it differs from Pinecone [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Vector, full-text and hybrid GA; rerank and auto-embedding preview |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | SSO, roles and auditing verified (B-L6-S001) plus the Atlas Admin API (B-REV-S028): rule 7 allows 4; SCIM and SLA not verified |
| Security and compliance | 4 | Strong platform certifications but scope rule (CP2 Q4): platform-level, preview features excluded |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Atlas on three clouds plus self-managed; no BYOC |
| Ecosystem | 4 | Official drivers and aggregation API; Voyage integration |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | Atlas mature; self-managed search GA only since c. July 2026 |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | Hourly Search Nodes; Community free; price tables conflict |
| Lock-in / portability | 2 | SSPL and proprietary Atlas; Voyage coupling |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.80 / 3.65** | |

**Capabilities.** Vector and full-text search inside MongoDB via $vectorSearch/$search with hybrid fusion GA; $rerank (Voyage, preview) and Automated Embedding (preview); GA on Atlas and self-managed Community/Enterprise Advanced 8.2+ [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S137: MongoDB Search and Vector Search Now Run Anywhere <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/mongodb-search-vector-search-now-run-anywhere> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S141: Context Engineering Has a Retrieval Issue: Introducing rerank-3 and Native Reranking (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-rerank-3-and-native-rerank> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S078: Unlocking AI Search: Introducing Automated Embedding in MongoDB Vector Search <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/unlocking-ai-search-introducing-automated-embedding-in-mongodb-vector-search> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S035: MongoDB Delivers Accurate AI Retrieval Wherever Enterprise Data Lives; Community Edition product page (MongoDB, Inc.) <https://investors.mongodb.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mongodb-delivers-accurate-ai-retrieval-wherever-enterprise-data> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- Transactional integration where documents already live in MongoDB [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Atlas ISO 27001:2022, SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, HITRUST, CSA STAR; FedRAMP Moderate for Gov [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S138: MongoDB Atlas Trust Center <https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform/trust> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- SSPL for self-managed; Atlas proprietary; Voyage-native features couple L6 and L7 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S137: MongoDB Search and Vector Search Now Run Anywhere <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/mongodb-search-vector-search-now-run-anywhere> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S141: Context Engineering Has a Retrieval Issue: Introducing rerank-3 and Native Reranking (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-rerank-3-and-native-rerank> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

- SOC 2 scope excludes preview features; Atlas log retention 30 days [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S027: SOC Compliance - MongoDB Atlas (MongoDB, Inc.) <https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform/trust/soc> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L6-S001: Manage Identity Providers (Atlas federated authentication); Guidance for Atlas Authorization; Set Up Database Auditing (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/manage-federated-auth/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]

**Choose when**

- MongoDB is the system of record for the documents being retrieved [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- MongoDB would be adopted only for retrieval [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Preview reranking or embedding would sit in regulated flows [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L6-pgvector, L6-elasticsearch, L6-pinecone

**Regulated-FS note.** Dedicated Search Nodes so CMK covers indexes; export audit logs to the firm's archive; Voyage features off until GA and Geography-scoped [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

*Rationale:* Distinctive object-storage design and per-namespace keys, but coarse key scoping, no ISO 27001, an Enterprise entry price well above peers and a proprietary API; author conflict disclosed and borderline calls resolved against it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Technical | 4 | Vector + BM25 + filters with namespace isolation at scale; cold latency trade-off |

| Security and compliance | 3 | SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, per-namespace CMEK, but no ISO 27001: maximum 3 |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | SaaS on three clouds, dedicated clusters and BYOC; no self-host |

| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Young company; named customers and profitability only via press |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | Published minimums and object-storage pricing, but the Enterprise tier needed for CMEK and private networking starts at US$4,096 per month with a 35% usage premium (Pinecone Enterprise from US$500); 3, resolved against the Anthropic-related item (CP3 review A) |

**Avoid when**
