# L5: Memory

## Zep (managed context-graph platform, 'Zep Cloud') and Graphiti (open-source temporal knowledge-graph framework) (`L5-zep`)

**Tier:** Tactical · **Flags:** Deprecated · **Original graphic label:** Zep – graph memory

*Rationale:* Technically the strongest memory model for audit and temporal reasoning; tier-gated compliance, a proprietary managed engine and pre-1.0 Graphiti keep it Tactical [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 5 | Bi-temporal graph, episodes with provenance, hybrid retrieval, users and threads: leading depth on the layer's memory-type questions |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | IdP sign-in, RBAC + ABAC and audit logs with one-year retention, plus a guaranteed SLA on Enterprise (A3-S107, A3-S089): rule 7 allows 4 (CP3 review A, consistent with Mistral OCR); condition: audit logs cover web-app actions only, not API or SDK calls |
| Security and compliance | 3 | SOC 2 Type II + HIPAA + BYOK on Enterprise; no ISO 27001 found (same calibration as Braintrust in L9) |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | SaaS and BYOC (AWS/GCP/Azure); Graphiti self-host; no supported self-host of Zep itself |
| Ecosystem | 4 | Broad framework integrations; Graphiti 31,529 stars; MCP server |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Graphiti pre-1.0 with frequent releases; SDK 4.0 beta; Community Edition deprecated; no acquisition found |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | Published credit pricing (Flex US$125, Flex Plus US$375 per month); Graphiti cost is graph DB + LLM ingestion |
| Lock-in / portability | 2 | Zep Cloud proprietary engine and API; Graphiti (Apache-2.0) is a partial exit with no documented migration |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.75 / 3.50** | |

**Capabilities.** Zep Cloud managed context-graph platform on a proprietary Context Graph Engine, with Graphiti (Apache-2.0) as the open-source temporal knowledge-graph framework: entities, facts with validity windows, episodes with provenance, communities; invalidation rather than deletion; hybrid semantic, keyword and graph retrieval [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S059: getzep/zep README: Zep Cloud Examples & Integrations (Zep AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getzep/zep/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Bi-temporal facts and per-episode provenance suit audit and how-facts-changed questions [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAA, BYOK and BYOC on Enterprise [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S089: Zep pricing <https://www.getzep.com/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S090: Zep Enterprise (and Emerging Companies programme page) <https://www.getzep.com/enterprise/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Right-to-be-forgotten and time-based retention purge (Zep Archive); EU residency on request; DPAs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S107: Zep docs: Governance (and Audit logging page, Zep Archive blog) <https://help.getzep.com/governance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Integrations with ADK, Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph, Strands and others; Graphiti MCP server [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S059: getzep/zep README: Zep Cloud Examples & Integrations (Zep AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getzep/zep/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Limitations and risks**

- Community Edition deprecated; Graphiti is the only OSS path [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S059: getzep/zep README: Zep Cloud Examples & Integrations (Zep AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getzep/zep/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S044: Announcing a New Direction for Zep's Open Source Strategy; Zep FAQ <https://blog.getzep.com/announcing-a-new-direction-for-zeps-open-source-strategy/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Compliance only on Enterprise, not Flex or Flex Plus [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S089: Zep pricing <https://www.getzep.com/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Audit logs cover web-app member actions, not API or SDK calls [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S107: Zep docs: Governance (and Audit logging page, Zep Archive blog) <https://help.getzep.com/governance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Graphiti pre-1.0; zep-cloud SDK 4.0 in beta [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S002: PyPI JSON metadata: zep-cloud (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/zep-cloud/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Proprietary graph engine in Zep Cloud; migration path to Graphiti not documented [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07] [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- Temporal validity and provenance of memory matter (mandate or terminology changes over time) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Graphiti self-hosted on Neo4j or Neptune for in-estate data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You need API-level audit logs from the vendor, ISO 27001, or a supported self-hosted full platform [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L5-mem0, L5-cognee, L5-gcp-vertex-memory-bank

**Regulated-FS note.** Prefer self-hosted Graphiti on an approved graph store and test that erasure removes invalidated facts and episodes; use Zep Cloud only on Enterprise with EU residency requested [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Technical | 4 | Memory, profiles, forgetting and hybrid RAG in one API |

## LangMem (`L5-langmem`)

**Tier:** Experimental · **Flags:** Not publicly verified · **Original graphic label:** LangMem – long-term

*Rationale:* Pre-1.0 and apparently stalled; useful as patterns, not as a dependency [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 3 | Extraction, consolidation and procedural memory, but no lifecycle or erasure features documented |
| Enterprise readiness | 2 | Rule 2: enables memory inside LangGraph; no commercial support for LangMem itself verified |
| Security and compliance | 2 | Rule 2: security policy, CVE handling and signed releases NPV |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Library runs wherever LangGraph and its store run, incl. in-estate |
| Ecosystem | 3 | LangGraph and LangChain only |
| Reliability and maturity | 1 | Pre-1.0 (0.0.x) with no release for about 11 months |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | MIT and free; cost is store plus extraction LLM; a stalled library may need in-house maintenance |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | MIT, but bound to LangGraph store abstractions |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **2.75 / 2.65** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rule 2 applied (self-hosted library; inherits host controls): security_compliance and enterprise_readiness capped at 4

**Capabilities.** MIT library of memory utilities for LangGraph: extraction, hot-path memory tools, background memory manager and prompt refinement (procedural memory); persists via LangGraph BaseStore [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Clear example of procedural memory (prompt refinement) and background consolidation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- No service to operate; MIT licence [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Limitations and risks**

- 0.0.30, no PyPI release since 27 October 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Tied to LangGraph store abstractions; InMemoryStore loses data on restart [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Whether LangChain has superseded it is not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Security and access control inherit entirely from the store and platform [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- Already on LangGraph and want reference patterns, accepting you may maintain the code [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You need a supported dependency [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L5-mem0, L5-zep, L5-letta

**Regulated-FS note.** Never let automatic prompt refinement change production prompts; route proposals through C5 change control [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

# L4: Tools, protocols and connectivity

## Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol (`L4-a2a`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** A2A – agent-to-agent

*Rationale:* Strategic, conditional: where cross-team or cross-vendor agent delegation is in scope (CP3 Q1); signed Agent Cards verified, and delegated authority scoped and revocable by the firm, because the protocol does not define it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 3 | Covers agent-to-agent interop well; not the main tool-invocation path and delegation semantics incomplete [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Open spec (rule 2): authenticated extended cards and declared security schemes; support via implementers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07] |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Rule 2 hygiene: modern OAuth flows, optional signing, undefined revocation semantics [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S079: A2A CHANGELOG (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07] |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | Implementations self-hostable anywhere [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| Ecosystem | 4 | 150+ organisations and cloud availability (April 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S025: A2A Protocol Surpasses 150 Organizations, Lands in Major Cloud Platforms, and Sees Enterprise Production Use in First Year (Linux Foundation) <https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/a2a-protocol-surpasses-150-organizations-lands-in-major-cloud-platforms-and-sees-enterprise-production-use-in-first-year> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | 1.0 only since March 2026 with breaking changes; foundation-hosted [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S079: A2A CHANGELOG (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S116: A2A joins AAIF's open agentic stack (17 Aug 2026) (Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)) <https://aaif.io/blog/a2a-joins-aaif> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Free specification; operations cost in implementations [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| Lock-in / portability | 5 | Apache-2.0 with neutral multi-vendor governance [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S075: PyPI JSON metadata: a2a-sdk (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/a2a-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S065: A2A GOVERNANCE.md (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/GOVERNANCE.md> accessed 2026-10-07] |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.60 / 3.70** | |

**Capabilities.** Open protocol (Apache-2.0) for communication between opaque agents: Agent Card discovery, messages, long-running tasks with streaming and push notifications; v1.0 adds multi-tenancy, multiple bindings, optional JWS-signed Agent Cards and modernised OAuth flows [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S030: A2A Protocol Ships v1.0: Production-Ready Standard (A2A Project (Linux Foundation)) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/announcing-1.0/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S079: A2A CHANGELOG (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Multi-vendor TSC of eight companies and AAIF Growth Stage status [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S065: A2A GOVERNANCE.md (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/GOVERNANCE.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S117: A New Chapter for A2A: Joining the Agentic AI Foundation (27 Aug 2026) (A2A Project) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/blog/2026/08/27/a-new-chapter-for-a2a-joining-the-agentic-ai-foundation/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Designed for delegated long-running tasks between agents [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Signed Agent Cards available [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Limitations and risks**

- Card signing optional; clients SHOULD verify only when present [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- No defined scope, validity or revocation semantics for authorisation obtained in AUTH_REQUIRED [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- 1.0 broke the interaction protocol; some SDKs lag [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S079: A2A CHANGELOG (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07] [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A3-S030: A2A Protocol Ships v1.0: Production-Ready Standard (A2A Project (Linux Foundation)) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/announcing-1.0/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Choose when**

- Agents owned by different teams or vendors must delegate work to each other [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- A deterministic workflow calling tools would do [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L4-mcp, C1-agentgateway, L4-aws-agentcore-gateway-identity

**Regulated-FS note.** Require signed Agent Cards and verify them; scope and revoke delegated authority in your own gateway and IdP [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Model Context Protocol (MCP) (`L4-mcp`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** MCP – tools standard

*Rationale:* Strategic, conditional: only behind a gateway with mandatory authorisation, an allow-list and pinned tool definitions. Tier set by the reader at Checkpoint 3 (CP3 Q1), treating MCP and its authorisation profile (C4-mcp-authorization) as one decision; FS 3.55 is below the 3.6 guide and security scores 2, which is why the condition is mandatory. Conflict of interest: MCP originated at Anthropic and the author is an Anthropic model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Covers tool invocation, enterprise authorisation and long-running tasks; security enforcement (allow-listing, signing) left outside the spec [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Open spec (rule 2): enables central IdP policy via EMA; no commercial support from the project itself [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| Security and compliance | 2 | Rule 2 hygiene: advisories are published with fixes (B-REVA-S006), but the specification leaves authorisation optional, has no tool-definition signing, carries a documented tool-poisoning attack class, and the TypeScript SDK had several High advisories in 2026, including one sending OAuth credentials to a server-chosen authorisation server [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S055: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S023: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning Attack on Real-World MCP Servers (arXiv (academic preprint; AAAI 2026)) <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.14925> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; B-REVA-S006: modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk security advisories (GitHub Advisory Database) (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/security/advisories> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Below A2A (optional card signing) on integrity; borderline 3/2 resolved against the Anthropic-originated item (CP3 review A) |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | Implementations run anywhere, including stdio locally and air-gapped [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| Ecosystem | 5 | De facto standard with broad client and launch-partner support [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S018: MCP joins the Agentic AI Foundation (9 Dec 2025) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2025-12-09-mcp-joins-agentic-ai-foundation/> accessed 2026-10-07] |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Foundation-hosted with a 12-month deprecation policy, but breaking changes in July 2026 and Registry still preview [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S042: modelcontextprotocol/registry (GitHub README) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |

**Choose when**

- One tool contract is needed across several agent frameworks and model vendors [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

**Nearest competitors:** OpenAPI tool definitions via gateway, L4-a2a, L4-aws-agentcore-gateway-identity

**Regulated-FS note.** Adopt the protocol, not the public ecosystem: internal servers behind a firm-owned gateway with authorisation mandatory and definitions hash-pinned; independent alternative is OpenAPI-described tools exposed through a gateway [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

- May 2026 incident: unauthorised access to internal systems; about 0.3% of connections and 5,241 API keys possibly exposed; token revocations and customer rotation required [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L4-S007: Composio May 2026 security incident update <https://composio.dev/blog/composio-may-2026-security-incident> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Security claims are vendor marketing only (V1 log section 4) [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Holds end users' OAuth tokens: high switching cost [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Managed cloud US-hosted; EU residency needs self-hosting [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S119: Composio: Two questions every security review asks us (and MCP gateway/governance pages) <https://composio.dev/blog/two-questions-every-security-review-asks-us> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- SDK pre-1.0 with 2.0 in beta [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S008: PyPI JSON metadata: composio (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/composio/json> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S098: PyPI JSON metadata: composio (0.25.0; 2.0.0b0 pre-release 31 Aug 2026) (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/composio/json> accessed 2026-10-08]

**Choose when**

- A low-risk internal productivity agent needs many SaaS connectors quickly, self-hosted [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- The agent touches client data or you cannot self-host in-region [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L4-aws-agentcore-gateway-identity, C4-okta-auth0-ai-agents, C1-kong-ai-gateway

**Regulated-FS note.** Do not let a third party hold staff OAuth tokens to firm systems in its multi-tenant cloud; if used, self-host and keep the token vault in your estate [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Capabilities.** Low-level stateful graph runtime (MIT) combining deterministic code and LLM decisions in one graph, with checkpointed durable execution, interrupts for human-in-the-loop, time travel, memory and streaming; managed runtime is LangSmith Deployment (formerly LangGraph Platform) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S118: LangGraph README (GitHub) (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S039: LangGraph Persistence / Durable execution / Interrupts - Docs by LangChain <https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/durable-execution> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S031: Product naming changes: LangSmith Deployment and LangSmith Studio (LangChain) <https://changelog.langchain.com/announcements/product-naming-changes-langsmith-deployment-and-langsmith-studio> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- Covers every L3 research question in one GA (1.x) framework with a no-breaking-changes commitment until 2.0 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S033: LangChain and LangGraph Agent Frameworks Reach v1.0 Milestones <https://www.langchain.com/blog/langchain-langgraph-1dot0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Deployment range from library to SaaS, BYOC, self-hosted and on-prem Kubernetes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S036: LangSmith Plans and Pricing (LangChain) <https://www.langchain.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S037: LangSmith Deployment - Docs by LangChain <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/deployment> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- Graph and checkpoint APIs are LangGraph-specific [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S039: LangGraph Persistence / Durable execution / Interrupts - Docs by LangChain <https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/durable-execution> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Three checkpoint deserialisation advisories in 2025-26, all patched; the checkpoint store is a security boundary [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S007: LangGraph security advisories (GitHub) and NVD entries (LangChain / GitHub / NIST NVD) <https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/security> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- LangSmith ISO 27001 claimed but scope unconfirmed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S034: LangSmith Regions FAQ (LangChain) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/regions-faq> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S035: LangChain Enterprise <https://www.langchain.com/enterprise> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S149: LangSmith Engine security - Docs by LangChain (with Trust Center, enterprise and shared-responsibility pages) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Full self-hosted platform needs the Enterprise plan [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S037: LangSmith Deployment - Docs by LangChain <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/deployment> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Choose when**

- You need deterministic workflow graphs with one or more LLM steps, durable checkpoints and approval interrupts [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Python or TypeScript teams standardising on one orchestration framework [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- The workflow is a single model call that needs no framework [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You cannot restrict write access to the checkpoint database [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L3-microsoft-agent-framework, L3-pydantic-ai, L3-google-adk, L3-temporal

**Avoid when**

**Capabilities.** Anthropic's agent harness SDK (formerly Claude Code SDK): embeds Claude Code's agent loop, built-in file/shell/web tools, hooks, subagents, MCP, permission modes and resumable/forkable sessions as a Python or TypeScript library; spawns one Claude Code CLI subprocess per session [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S027: Agent SDK overview - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S122: Hosting the Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S028: Migrate to Claude Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/migration-guide> accessed 2026-10-07]. **Strengths**

- Permission modes and hooks give fine-grained tool approval [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S027: Agent SDK overview - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Strong fit for code- and file-centric autonomous tasks [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Limitations and risks**

- Python package classified Alpha; 0.x versioning [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: claude-agent-sdk (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Claude models only, via Claude API, Bedrock or Google Cloud [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: claude-agent-sdk (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S122: Hosting the Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Use governed by Anthropic Commercial Terms despite the MIT repository licence [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S092: Claude Agent SDK (Python) LICENSE (Anthropic) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S048: Agent SDK overview (License and terms section) (Anthropic) <https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-08]
- One long-lived subprocess per session; transcripts on local disk unless a SessionStore is configured [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S122: Hosting the Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting> accessed 2026-10-07]

- No deterministic workflow engine [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S027: Agent SDK overview - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Choose when**

- A sandboxed autonomous sub-task (e.g. code or document manipulation) inside a firm-owned workflow, where Claude is already an approved model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You need model portability or a deterministic workflow engine [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- A regulated process would run on an Alpha-classified dependency [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L3-openai-agents-sdk, L3-langgraph, L3-pydantic-ai

**Regulated-FS note.** Run only in sandboxed containers with network controls, under a workflow engine that owns state and approvals; independent alternatives are LangGraph and Pydantic AI [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Choose when**

**Avoid when**

**Limitations and risks**

- Pre-1.0 (v0.7) and sandbox stage [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Vendor support is Technology Preview, not covered by production SLAs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S002: Supported platforms for Distributed Inference with llm-d (Red Hat AI 3) <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ai/3/html/supported_product_and_hardware_configurations/llmd-supported-platforms_supported-configurations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Needs Kubernetes and data-centre accelerators [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; B-L2-S002: Supported platforms for Distributed Inference with llm-d (Red Hat AI 3) <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ai/3/html/supported_product_and_hardware_configurations/llmd-supported-platforms_supported-configurations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]

**Choose when**

- Kubernetes is your platform standard and you are building a multi-model internal inference service [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You need production-supported software now [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S002: Supported platforms for Distributed Inference with llm-d (Red Hat AI 3) <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ai/3/html/supported_product_and_hardware_configurations/llmd-supported-platforms_supported-configurations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Volumes do not justify multi-replica routing [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L2-nvidia-dynamo, L2-vllm, KServe

# L1: Foundation models

## OpenAI GPT model family (GPT-6: Astra, Sol, Luna; GPT-6.1 Sol), plus GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna and open-weight gpt-oss (`L1-openai`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** OpenAI – GPT-6

*Rationale:* Broadest evidenced lineup, two hyperscaler routes plus first-party EU processing, product-scoped SOC 2 and ISO 27001; concentration is managed by pairing with a second vendor, not by avoiding OpenAI [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 5 | Covers every plan §5 L1 question on primary evidence: frontier, mid and small tiers, reasoning, image input, coding, a specialist cyber line and Apache-2.0 open weights (A5-S002, A5-S005, A5-S008). Benchmarks not used. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | First-party SSO/RBAC/audit and support terms are NPV; GPT-6 is consumed in-tenant through Bedrock and Foundry, so the hyperscaler presumption gives 4 (rule 6). Platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service. |
| Security and compliance | 4 | SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 within API scope, ZDR and first-party EU residency (A5-S006, A5-S007, V2-S062); not 5 because ISO 42001 scope does not name the API and CMK is not verified (rule 8). |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | First-party SaaS (US, EU, UK-storage endpoints), Bedrock, Foundry, and self-hosted/air-gapped gpt-oss; 4 not 5 because the frontier tiers cannot be self-hosted and gpt-oss dates from August 2025. |
| Ecosystem | 5 | The OpenAI API shape is the de facto interface: other vendors publish OpenAI-compatible endpoints (A5-S010, A5-S077, A5-S038); official SDKs; two hyperscalers. |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | Years of production use and a published deprecation policy (B-L1-S001); fast tier churn (GPT-5.6 in July, GPT-6 in September 2026) and the Astra GA conflict keep it at 4. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Transparent per-tier pricing (Luna US$0.10/US$0.50, Sol US$2/US$10, Astra US$10/US$50 per 1M) with 50% batch discount (A5-S004); competitive, not uniquely efficient. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Proprietary frontier API on a de facto standard interface, on two non-OpenAI clouds, with Apache-2.0 gpt-oss as a portability option. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **4.25 / 4.05** | |

**Capabilities.** Tiered proprietary family: GPT-6 Astra (gated flagship, introduced 3 September 2026), GPT-6 Sol and Luna (22 September 2026), GPT-6.1 Sol (29 September 2026), with GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna still offered; all GPT-6 tiers are reasoning models with text and image input; Daybreak cyber models in limited availability on Bedrock; open-weight gpt-oss-120b/20b under Apache 2.0 (August 2025) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S001: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol / GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna (with help-centre preview article and API changelog) (OpenAI) <https://openai.com/index/previewing-gpt-5-6-sol/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; **Strengths**

- Complete tier ladder (frontier, mid, small) plus Apache-2.0 open weights, so one vendor covers every portfolio tier except sovereign self-hosted frontier [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S002: GPT-6 Astra: A new generation of intelligence (plus release notes, Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 for everyone) (OpenAI) <https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A5-S005: Introducing gpt-oss (and gpt-oss-safeguard; help-centre open-weight article) (OpenAI) <https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-oss/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

- First-party EU residency: eu.api.openai.com stores and processes in region (new projects, with Modified Abuse Monitoring or ZDR) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S006: Data controls in the OpenAI platform (with Enterprise privacy, EU/UK data residency announcements) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S079: Data controls in the OpenAI platform (with help article 'Data residency for the OpenAI API'; 'Expanding data residency access') <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- SOC 2 Type 2 for the API Platform and ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701 covering the API [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S007: OpenAI Trust Portal (with Security and privacy at OpenAI; Enterprise privacy FAQ) <https://trust.openai.com/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S062: OpenAI Trust Portal (with openai.com/security-and-privacy) <https://trust.openai.com/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- Frontier tiers are closed-weight and API-only; fine-tuning is not supported for Astra [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S003: OpenAI announces rollout of GPT-6 Astra model (with Axios and OpenRouter results) (CNBC) <https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/03/open-ai-astra-gpt-6-cyber.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

- UK endpoint stores data in the UK but does not process there [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S006: Data controls in the OpenAI platform (with Enterprise privacy, EU/UK data residency announcements) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S079: Data controls in the OpenAI platform (with help article 'Data residency for the OpenAI API'; 'Expanding data residency access') <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Bedrock Astra is in-region only in us-east-1 and us-west-2 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S008: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra / GPT-6 Sol and Luna generally available on Amazon Bedrock (AWS) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/09/openai-gpt-6-astra-on-amazon-bedrock/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- ISO/IEC 42001 scope wording does not name the API Platform; CMK and first-party SSO/SCIM/RBAC were not verified [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S062: OpenAI Trust Portal (with openai.com/security-and-privacy) <https://trust.openai.com/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Preview models may be retired on about 2 weeks' notice [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L1-S001: Deprecations (OpenAI API docs) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Not on Google Cloud except gpt-oss [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S027: Generative AI pricing - Google Cloud (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI) <https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Choose when**

- You need a primary or fallback frontier vendor available in-tenant on Azure or AWS with a first-party EU residency option [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You want one vendor relationship that also supplies a small classification tier (Luna) and a self-hostable open-weight model (gpt-oss) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- Google Cloud is the only permitted cloud and you need GPT-6 tiers [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You need UK in-country processing [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You would use Promptfoo, now announced as part of OpenAI, as the only independent test of an OpenAI-based system [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L1-anthropic, L1-google-gemini, L1-mistral

**Regulated-FS note.** Consume via Microsoft Foundry EU Data Zone or the EU first-party endpoint with ZDR or Modified Abuse Monitoring; pin dated snapshots, track the deprecations page, and keep a second vendor qualified as the SS2/21 exit route [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Anthropic Claude model family (Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5; restricted Claude Mythos 5.1) (`L1-anthropic`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** Claude – Opus 5.5

*Rationale:* Strategic, conditional: consumed only through a hyperscaler EU or UK region (Bedrock regional endpoint or Google Cloud EU), as one of two frontier and mid-tier vendors with a non-Anthropic fallback qualified on the same evaluation suite, not as the sole frontier model; independent alternatives are OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 3.8 Flash and Mistral Medium 3.5. FS 3.80 with no criterion below 3. Tier and neutral scoring set by the reader at Checkpoint 4 (CP4-1); the author's pipeline had resolved three borderline scores against Anthropic. Security 5 and cost 4 are the neutral rubric values identified in CP4 review C (previously 4 and 3). The first-party residency gap and the June 2026 Fable 5 suspension remain factual weaknesses and are stated as conditions. Conflict of interest: the author is an Anthropic model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Four GA tiers with 1M context, reasoning, image input and coding (A5-S010); no open-weight, audio or image-output models and no GA specialist line, so fewer plan §5 questions covered than OpenAI or Google; borderline 4/5 resolved against Anthropic (conflict rule). CP4 review C found 4 is also the neutral value on peers; unchanged at CP4. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | Workspaces, Admin API, Compliance API / Activity Feed and WIF verified (A5-S013, A5-S018) plus in-tenant hyperscaler routes (rule 6); not 5 because SSO/SCIM detail and SLA are NPV. Platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service. |
| Security and compliance | 5 | Product-scoped SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 covering the API and Claude in Bedrock and Google Cloud, plus CMEK in the admin console (A5-S021, V2-S063, A5-S013), meet the rule-8 test for 5. Set to 5, the neutral rubric value, by the reader at Checkpoint 4 (CP4-1; previously held at 4 against Anthropic). Residency and ZDR are optional extras under the anchor, so the absence of a first-party EU/UK inference geography (V2-S075) and the top tier's conflicting ZDR position (A5-S023, A5-S016) are carried as tier conditions, not score deductions; the Azure-hosted Foundry deployment is still 'In-Process Q4 2026' for certification (V2-S063). |
| Deployment flexibility | 3 | First-party SaaS plus Bedrock, Google Cloud, Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS; no self-hosting or on-premises (A5-S010). |
| Ecosystem | 4 | Three hyperscalers and an OpenAI SDK compatibility endpoint (A5-S010); the API itself is not the de facto standard; borderline 4/5 resolved against Anthropic. CP4 review C found 4 is also the neutral value on peers; unchanged at CP4. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Published retirement commitments (A5-S010) are positive, but top-tier access was suspended 12 June to 1 July 2026 (V2-S004), four models shipped in five weeks, and the D.C. Circuit upheld a federal supply-chain-risk designation (A5-S084). |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Transparent; list prices equal OpenAI's at every tier (Fable 5.1 = Astra US$10/US$50; Sonnet 5.5 = GPT-6.1 Sol US$2/US$10; Haiku 5.5 = Luna US$0.10/US$0.50 per 1M) with a 50% batch discount (A5-S011, A5-S004), and OpenAI scores 4. The 10% regional premium does not hold peers at 3 (Mistral and Grok score 4), and the dearer recommended default (Opus 5.5, US$4/US$20) is a deployment choice, not a vendor price. Set to 4, the neutral rubric value, by the reader at Checkpoint 4 (CP4-1; previously 3). |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Proprietary API with no open weights, but on three clouds and with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so a gateway can switch it out. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.85 / 3.80** | |

**Capabilities.** Proprietary Claude family: Claude Fable 5.1 (top GA tier, 1 September 2026), Opus 5.5 (22 September 2026; Anthropic's recommended starting point), Sonnet 5.5 (28 September 2026) and Haiku 5.5 (7 October 2026); Mythos 5.1 is the same model as Fable 5.1 with looser safeguards for trusted-access programmes only; all four GA models have adaptive thinking, text and image input, text output, 1M-token context and 128K output; no open weights [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S010: Models overview - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S012: Anthropic Newsroom <https://www.anthropic.com/news> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S016: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S019: Introducing Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S020: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5 (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S066: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1> accessed 2026-10-08]. **Choose when**

- You need a second frontier vendor that is available in-tenant on whichever hyperscaler is primary, including Google Cloud where OpenAI's GPT-6 is not offered [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Long-context (1M tokens on every tier) drafting or agentic coding is the main workload [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- EU or UK processing must be contracted with the model vendor itself rather than through a hyperscaler [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- The firm has US defence-contract exposure and its legal team has not assessed the supply-chain-risk designation [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You need a self-hostable model from the same vendor [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** L1-openai, L1-google-gemini, L1-mistral

## DeepSeek V4 family (DeepSeek-V4-Pro; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, which replaced V4-Flash in the API) (`L1-deepseek`)

**Tier:** Tactical · **Flags:** Not recommended · **Original graphic label:** DeepSeek – V4

*Rationale:* Tactical, conditional: self-hosted MIT weights or Microsoft Foundry in-tenant only; the 'Not recommended' flag applies to DeepSeek's hosted API (PRC storage, unremediated Garante limitation) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Enterprise readiness | 4 | 4 only for the Microsoft Foundry route, where Azure sells DeepSeek V4 directly and processes it in-tenant in the customer's geography (rule 6; A5-S087); DeepSeek's own API has no verified SSO/RBAC/audit and would be capped at 2. Hosting caveat (CP4-3): on Azure, Microsoft Foundry's Kimi K3 and GLM-5.x run on Fireworks outside the customer tenant, while DeepSeek V4 is sold directly and processed in-tenant (A5-S087). Kept at 4 by the reader at Checkpoint 4 (CP4-3). Platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service. |
| Security and compliance | 1 | Hosted API meets anchor 1: no verified certification, PRC storage (A5-S062) and an unremediated Garante limitation (A5-S048, V2-S023). Self-hosted weights would score about 3 under rule 2 (inherits host controls), with CAISI's hijacking findings (A5-S049) as a model-behaviour risk. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Self-host and air-gap possible (MIT), Foundry in-tenant, own SaaS; 4 not 5 because the vendor SaaS is PRC-only and V4 is not on Bedrock or Google Cloud (A5-S086, A5-S027). |
| Ecosystem | 4 | Broad open-serving support and third-party hosts (A5-S039, A5-S044, A5-S087). |
| Reliability and maturity | 2 | Phase-out of V4-Pro announced 10 September and reversed 17 September 2026 (V2-S013); certifications and support NPV. |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | Weights free (MIT) but V4-Pro needs a large multi-GPU cluster; hosted prices are aggregator-level and not used (V2 §4 item 3). |
| Lock-in / portability | 4 | MIT weights mean no model lock-in once self-hosted; jurisdictional exit risk is captured in security and tier. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.25 / 3.15** | |

*Rationale:* Tactical, conditional: self-hosted GLM-5.3-Flash (MIT) only, after sanctions review; Entity List status and unverified data terms rule out the hosted API [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Large agentic/coding model, a multimodal MIT Flash tier and an image model; CAISI's independent assessment places GLM-5.3 near the frontier on cyber tasks (A5-S052). |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | The Bedrock (AWS-operated) route gives the hyperscaler presumption (rule 6): GLM 5.3 cross-Region only from 5 October 2026, GLM 5 in-Region in London (A5-S086). Hosting caveat (CP4-3): on Azure, Microsoft Foundry's Kimi K3 and GLM-5.x run on Fireworks outside the customer tenant, while DeepSeek V4 is sold directly and processed in-tenant (A5-S087). The Azure route therefore does not support this score, and Z.ai API controls are NPV (would be 2). Kept at 4 by the reader at Checkpoint 4 (CP4-3). Platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service. |
| Security and compliance | 2 | Certifications NPV (cap 2); Singapore processing and DPA conflict (A5-S073). |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Own API, three hyperscalers (London in-Region for GLM 5), Mistral platform, self-host and on-premises. |
| Ecosystem | 3 | Present on many platforms, but the current GLM-5.3 reaches them via cross-Region or pass-through routes; Mistral retires GLM 5.2 on its platform on 31 October 2026 (B-L1-S002). |
| Reliability and maturity | 2 | Entity List exposure is a continuity risk for any commercial relationship (A5-S072); maturity and support NPV. |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | MIT Flash weights are cheap to run; GLM-5.3 needs multi-GPU serving; hosted prices not decision inputs (V2 §4 item 3). |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | MIT for Flash; MIT-style grant with a MaaS condition for GLM-5.3 (rule 4). |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rule 2 basis: self-hosted open-core software with commercial support; NPV cap not applied

**Capabilities.** Open-core Python SDK and proxy exposing 100+ providers through an OpenAI-format API, with virtual keys, budgets per key/user/team/customer, TPM/RPM limits, fallbacks, exact and semantic caching, pre/during/post-call guardrail hooks and logging callbacks; the same proxy fronts MCP servers and A2A agents [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S051: LiteLLM README (GitHub) (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Widest provider coverage and the de facto open-source gateway; basis of AWS's own multi-provider Guidance [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S022: Guidance for Multi-Provider Generative AI Gateway on AWS; Implementing resilience patterns with Amazon Bedrock and LLM gateway (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/solutions/guidance/multi-provider-generative-ai-gateway-on-aws/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- One control plane for LLM, MCP and A2A traffic with shared auth, limits and spend tracking [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- MIT core and OpenAI-format API keep the application exit cheap [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S001: litellm - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/litellm/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Limitations and risks**

- PyPI supply-chain compromise on 24 March 2026 (1.82.7 and 1.82.8) via CI credentials; clean v1.83.0 released 30 March 2026 (US time) from a rebuilt pipeline [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S008: Security Update: Suspected Supply Chain Incident (and Security Townhall Updates) (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-update-march-2026> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S009: v1.83.0 - Official Release (Post Supply Chain Incident) (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/release_notes/v1.83.0/v1-83-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S027: LiteLLM PyPI supply chain attack (with NetSPI, Comet, Snyk/Datadog reporting) (FutureSearch) <https://futuresearch.ai/blog/litellm-pypi-supply-chain-attack/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; V2-S028: PyPI JSON API: litellm, guardrails-ai, presidio-analyzer, nemoguardrails, llamafirewall, langfuse, promptfoo, modelscan, picklescan, fickling, safetensors, mode <https://pypi.org/pypi/litellm/json> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Several controls fail open or are off by default: max_budget without a database, prompt-injection guardrails off, admin key bypasses budgets; A2A agents open to all callers until an allowlist is set [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- SSO beyond 5 users, RBAC, SCIM and audit logs need the commercial licence; pricing model described inconsistently [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S007: LiteLLM pricing / Enterprise / Audit Logs docs (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://www.litellm.ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- ISO 27001 recertification not confirmed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S108: Our Updated SOC 2 Type 2 Report Is Available; LiteLLM + Vanta: SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 Recertification; Data Privacy and Security; Trust Center (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/soc2-type-2-report> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Choose when**

- You want a self-hosted, provider-neutral gateway for LLM, MCP and A2A traffic and will run it as a hardened internal service [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You will buy the Enterprise licence for SSO, RBAC and audit logs [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You cannot pin versions, mirror packages and verify signed images [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You would run the open edition without a database and accept fail-open budgets [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C1-kong-ai-gateway, C1-portkey, C1-agentgateway

**Regulated-FS note.** Treat as a Tier-1 internal service: install only from a private mirror with pinned hashes, deploy the cosign-signed images, run fail-closed configuration and buy Enterprise for audit evidence [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Microsoft Entra Agent ID (`C4-entra-agent-id`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Strategic, conditional: where Entra is the workforce IdP; FS 3.50 is below the usual 3.6 because deployment and cost score 2, accepted because agent identity must live in the same directory as the delegating humans [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 5 | Blueprints, agent identities, OBO and autonomous flows, Conditional Access, governance, ID Protection and audit for agents. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | Hyperscaler presumption (CP2 Q1): platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service; access controls and audit logs for agents also verified (A6-S058). |
| Security and compliance | 4 | Entra ID in ISO 27001 (commercial) and FedRAMP High scope; commercial SOC 2 scope does not name it; Agent ID and Agent 365 not named separately (scope rule, 4). |
| Deployment flexibility | 2 | Microsoft cloud service only. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | Guides for Bedrock and n8n agents, MCP and A2A, workload identity federation. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | GA April 2026; parts still preview. |
| Cost / TCO | 2 | Agent 365 licence needed for security features; prices not verified. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Standard OAuth/OIDC tokens, but proprietary agent constructs and licensing. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.55 / 3.50** | |

**Capabilities.** Agent identity platform in Microsoft Entra: agent identity blueprints, agent identities, agent users, owners/sponsors/managers; OAuth client_credentials for autonomous agents, jwt-bearer On-Behalf-Of, refresh_token for long-running delegated work, no interactive flows; Conditional Access, ID Governance access packages, ID Protection, network controls and sign-in/audit logs extended to agents; supports MCP, A2A and non-Microsoft agents via sidecar SDK or workload identity federation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S057: What is Microsoft Entra Agent ID? (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/what-is-microsoft-entra-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S058: What's new in Microsoft Entra Agent ID (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/whats-new-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S060: Authentication protocols for agents (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/agent-oauth-protocols.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. GA April 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S032: Microsoft Entra releases and announcements (with What's new in Entra Agent ID; Entra blog 'Build AI agents for production with secure identities from day one';  <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/whats-new> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- Agent identity in the same directory as the human principals, so OBO delegation and Conditional Access apply natively [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Explicit sponsor/owner model and access packages for agents [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S057: What is Microsoft Entra Agent ID? (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/what-is-microsoft-entra-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S058: What's new in Microsoft Entra Agent ID (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/whats-new-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Standard OAuth flows; no interactive flows for agent entities [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S060: Authentication protocols for agents (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/agent-oauth-protocols.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Entra ID in ISO 27001 and FedRAMP High scope [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C4-S008: ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2 offering pages (Microsoft Compliance) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/compliance/regulatory/offering-iso-27001> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A6-S056: Azure services in FedRAMP and DoD audit scope (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/azure-government/compliance/azure-services-in-fedramp-auditscope.md> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Limitations and risks**

- Microsoft-specific constructs (blueprints, agent users) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S057: What is Microsoft Entra Agent ID? (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/what-is-microsoft-entra-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Some admin-centre wizards still preview; registry converging into Agent 365 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S058: What's new in Microsoft Entra Agent ID (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/whats-new-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Agent 365 list prices not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- Entra is the workforce IdP [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

## MCP Authorization (MCP specification 2026-07-28) plus Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension (`C4-mcp-authorization`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Strategic, conditional: only behind a gateway with mandatory authorisation, an allow-list and pinned tool definitions. Tier set by the reader at Checkpoint 3 (CP3 Q1): MCP (L4-mcp) and its authorisation profile are one decision. FS 3.45 and reliability 2 (IETF drafts, four breaking revisions) are why the condition includes pinning the specification revision at the gateway. Conflict of interest: MCP originated at Anthropic and the author is an Anthropic model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Strong agent-to-tool contract (audience binding, PRM, issuer validation, EMA); optional and silent on fine-grained policy. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Rule 2: EMA lets the corporate IdP govern access; enterprise features come from implementations. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Rule 2 hygiene: private advisory reporting and documented trust model (B-C4-S004); optional authorisation and draft dependencies keep it at 3. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Implementation-dependent; usable in self-hosted and managed gateways. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | Implemented by AWS AgentCore Gateway, Kong AI Gateway, Okta XAA and Azure API Management; MCP itself is the de facto tool protocol (L4 scores it 5), but authorisation is optional and adoption of the authorisation profile across servers is not publicly verified, so 4. |
| Reliability and maturity | 2 | Four breaking revisions in about 16 months; OAuth 2.1 still draft. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Free specification; implementation and re-certification on each revision cost effort. |
| Lock-in / portability | 4 | Open specification under Linux Foundation hosting; maintainer concentration at one vendor. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.50 / 3.45** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rule 2 (self-hosted software / open specification): enterprise_readiness and security_compliance capped at 4; NPV cap not applied; inherits host controls

**Capabilities.** Authorisation profile of OAuth 2.1 (still an IETF draft) for MCP: server as resource server with Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728), PKCE, audience-bound tokens via Resource Indicators (RFC 8707), token passthrough forbidden; 2026-07-28 adds RFC 9207 issuer validation and issuer-bound clients and deprecates Dynamic Client Registration; Enterprise-Managed Authorization (ID-JAG) extension Stable. Authorisation is OPTIONAL [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S034: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization security considerations (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S032: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Key Changes (changelog) (Model Context Protocol project (Agentic AI Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S035: MCP extension: Enterprise-Managed Authorization (overview) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/extensions/auth/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S079: MCP ext-auth: Enterprise-Managed Authorization specification (Stable) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth/main/specification/stable/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Audience binding and the ban on token passthrough address the confused-deputy problem [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S034: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization security considerations (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Enterprise IdP decides which MCP servers an employee can use (EMA/ID-JAG) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S035: MCP extension: Enterprise-Managed Authorization (overview) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/extensions/auth/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S079: MCP ext-auth: Enterprise-Managed Authorization specification (Stable) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth/main/specification/stable/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Implemented by AgentCore Gateway, Kong and Okta XAA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S021: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing; AgentCore GA announcement (Oct 2025); AgentCore Gateway docs (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S017: Kong AI Gateway changelog; Kong Gateway changelog; AI Proxy Advanced plugin docs (Kong Inc.) <https://developer.konghq.com/ai-gateway/changelog/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S099: Okta brings first-class identity to AI agents with Agent SSO; Okta Introduces Agent SSO for Cross App Access (XAA) (Okta, Inc.) <https://www.okta.com/newsroom/press-releases/okta-brings-first-class-identity-to-ai-agents-with-agent-sso/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Hosted by the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation) since 9 December 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S018: MCP joins the Agentic AI Foundation (9 Dec 2025) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2025-12-09-mcp-joins-agentic-ai-foundation/> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Limitations and risks**

- Authorisation is OPTIONAL in MCP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Frequent breaking revisions: 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, 2026-07-28 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S021: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing; AgentCore GA announcement (Oct 2025); AgentCore Gateway docs (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Several dependencies are IETF drafts, including OAuth 2.1 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S079: MCP ext-auth: Enterprise-Managed Authorization specification (Stable) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth/main/specification/stable/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Both Lead Maintainers are Anthropic staff [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S082: Expanding the MCP Maintainer Team (8 Apr 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-04-08-maintainer-update/> accessed 2026-10-07]; the author is an Anthropic model (conflict of interest)
- Security policy states clients trust configured servers and that access control is the server developer's responsibility [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C4-S004: Model Context Protocol Security Policy (SECURITY.md) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08]

**Choose when**

- MCP is the firm's tool protocol [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- Tools are exposed as REST/OpenAPI behind a gateway, where plain OAuth 2.0 resource-server patterns suffice [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** Gateway-native tool auth (Kong, AgentCore Gateway, Azure APIM credential manager), C4-okta-auth0-ai-agents, OAuth 2.0 resource-server pattern for REST tools

**Regulated-FS note.** Strategic, conditional, and mandatory wherever MCP is used (CP3 Q1): make authorisation mandatory by firm policy, pin the spec revision at the gateway, and require EMA so the corporate IdP mediates access; the durable controls are the IdP and the gateway PDP, which keep working if the tool protocol changes [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

# C5: Prompt and configuration management

## LangSmith prompt management (Prompts, Prompt Hub) (`C5-langsmith-prompts`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Strategic only in a LangSmith/LangGraph estate, with GitHub sync enabled as the exit route; otherwise Tactical [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Commits, diffs, environments, promotion, rollback history, owners, webhooks and Git sync; no documented percentage rollout or user segmentation. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | Organisation and workspace roles, custom RBAC and per-prompt owners; Enterprise SSO, ABAC and support SLA from the platform record; SCIM not documented. |
| Security and compliance | 4 | SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, HIPAA BAA on Enterprise; no CMK/BYOK documented, so not 5. |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | SaaS in US, EU and APAC regions, BYOC on AWS, self-hosted and air-gapped self-host on Enterprise. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | LangChain ecosystem, langchain-prompty integration, webhooks and GitHub sync. |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | GA since 2023, independent and funded (US$125M Series B, October 2025). |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | Per-seat plus per-trace pricing; heavy self-host footprint. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Proprietary service, but prompt text syncs to GitHub, so lock-in is lower than for LangSmith traces (L9 scores 2). |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **4.00 / 3.95** | |

**Capabilities.** Prompts stored as a commit history with diffs; reserved Staging and Production environments assigned by promotion; per-environment rollback history; 'owners only' mode restricting who may tag, promote or delete; webhooks on every commit; synchronisation of prompts with a GitHub repository; public prompt hub [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- The most complete change-control workflow among the registries profiled: commits, diffs, promotion, rollback history and prompt owners [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- GitHub synchronisation gives a documented export path and lets Git remain the record [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Webhooks on commit can trigger CI evaluation and change tickets [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022 and HIPAA; US, EU (Netherlands) and APAC regions; BYOC on AWS, self-host and air-gapped self-host on Enterprise [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S077: LangSmith docs: Regions FAQ (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/regions-faq.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S036: LangSmith Regions FAQ - Docs by LangChain (LangChain, Inc.) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/regions-faq> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S126: LangSmith Engine security - Docs by LangChain (LangChain, Inc.) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S034: Set up LangSmith (deployment options) - Docs by LangChain (LangChain, Inc.) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/platform-setup> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- Proprietary service for prompt storage and promotion [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S079: LangSmith docs: Self-hosted (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/self-hosted.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- No EU legal entity for contracting [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S077: LangSmith docs: Regions FAQ (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/regions-faq.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Self-hosting is an Enterprise add-on with a heavy footprint (Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Redis, ClickHouse) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S079: LangSmith docs: Self-hosted (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/self-hosted.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S034: Set up LangSmith (deployment options) - Docs by LangChain (LangChain, Inc.) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/platform-setup> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Platform increasingly bundles the LangChain agent runtime [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S039: Everything we shipped at Interrupt (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/blog/interrupt-2026-overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Choose when**

- LangSmith is already the L9 platform and LangGraph the orchestration standard [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Product owners need a UI promotion and rollback workflow while engineering keeps Git as the record via sync [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You want the prompt registry separated from the agent runtime vendor [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Contracting with an EU legal entity is a requirement [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C5-langfuse-prompts, C5-promptlayer, C5-prompts-as-code

**Regulated-FS note.** Enable owners-only mode on production prompts, route promotion through a service identity triggered after the eval gate, and use GitHub sync so that the approved prompt text also lives in the firm's repository [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
