## Langfuse Prompt Management (a capability of the Langfuse platform) (`C5-langfuse-prompts`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** Acquired · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Strategic only where Langfuse is the L9 platform of record and the Enterprise licence is bought for protected labels, RBAC and audit logs; otherwise Tactical [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Versions, environment/tenant/experiment labels, client caching, loud failure on missing labels and trace linkage; no documented approval workflow, Git sync or percentage rollout. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | Rule 7, aligned with the CP2 rework of L9 Langfuse (4): SSO, project-level RBAC, audit logs, SCIM and the Org Management API verified [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S074: Langfuse docs: Enterprise License Key (self-hosted) (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/self-hosting/license-key.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S033: Self-Hosted Pricing - Langfuse (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://langfuse.com/pricing-self-host> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Enterprise-licensed when self-hosted, which is a stated condition of the tier; SLA terms not published. |
| Security and compliance | 4 | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 with annual audits, DPA, EU region on Cloud; no CMK/BYOK documented, so not 5. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | SaaS (US, EU, JP, HIPAA regions), self-hosted in any region and fully offline; kept at 4 for consistency with L9 because vendor-managed BYOC is not documented (see scoring notes). |
| Ecosystem | 4 | Open-source SDKs in Python and JS/TS, OTel-based platform, wide adoption of the parent platform; prompt API is Langfuse-specific. |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | Platform at v4, frequent SDK releases (4.17.0 on 5 October 2026); ownership changed to ClickHouse in January 2026 with no planned licence change. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | MIT core free; the governance controls this control needs are in the paid Enterprise tier. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Base 4 (MIT, self-hostable, prompts are text) reduced by 1 for the 2026 ownership change. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.95 / 3.85** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* CP3 review: enterprise readiness raised from 3 to 4 to match the CP2-reworked L9 Langfuse score (rule 7: all three controls plus SCIM and an admin API)

**Capabilities.** Prompt registry inside the Langfuse platform: every prompt version gets an immutable version ID; labels (production, staging, tenant or experiment) select which version the SDK fetches; SDKs cache prompts client-side; prompt versions are linked to traces so quality and cost can be analysed by version; protected prompt labels restrict who may move a production label (Enterprise) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S074: Langfuse docs: Enterprise License Key (self-hosted) (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/self-hosting/license-key.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Version-to-trace linkage answers 'which prompt version produced this output' inside the same store that holds the evaluation evidence (see L9) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Client-side SDK caching keeps the registry off the hot path [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- A missing label returns an error rather than silently serving another version, so a mislabelled environment fails loudly [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- MIT core; self-hosted or Cloud with SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and an EU (Ireland) region [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S073: Langfuse Security and Compliance overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/security/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S074: Langfuse docs: Enterprise License Key (self-hosted) (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/self-hosting/license-key.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Limitations and risks**

- Protected prompt labels, project-level RBAC, audit logs and SCIM need an Enterprise licence key when self-hosted, so segregation of duties on production prompts is a paid feature [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S074: Langfuse docs: Enterprise License Key (self-hosted) (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/self-hosting/license-key.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- No native pull-request style approval or Git synchronisation documented in the fact base [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Owned by ClickHouse (acquisition announced 16 January 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S075: Langfuse README (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S041: ClickHouse welcomes Langfuse (with langfuse.com 'Langfuse joins ClickHouse', Orrick) <https://clickhouse.com/blog/clickhouse-acquires-langfuse-open-source-llm-observability> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Langfuse-specific prompt API and SDK [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Choose when**

- Langfuse is already the L9 platform of record and you want prompt versions and traces in one place [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You need a self-hosted registry inside the estate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You will not buy the Enterprise licence, because without protected labels any project member with write access can move the production label [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Your change process requires approvals to happen in the source-control system [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C5-langsmith-prompts, C5-promptlayer, C5-prompts-as-code

**Regulated-FS note.** Use as the runtime delivery and trace-linkage layer, fed by CI from Git after the eval gate; make the production label protected and restrict label moves to the release pipeline's identity [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Prompts-as-code pattern: Git-versioned prompt files (Prompty, Dotprompt) tested by config-driven evals (e.g. Promptfoo) (`C5-prompts-as-code`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** Acquired · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* The only option whose change record lives in the firm's own controls and survives any vendor exit; the Acquired flag refers to Promptfoo as the example eval CLI, which is replaceable [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 3 | Versioning, review, diff and CI evaluation are strong; runtime delivery, segmentation, instant rollback and trace linkage have to be built. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | Rubric rule 2: scored on what the pattern enables in-estate. It inherits the firm's source-control SSO, RBAC, mandatory approvals and audit; scored at the rule 2 maximum of 4 (no commercial support for the formats) because approval and audit are the whole function of this control, unlike OPA or OpenLineage (3). |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Rubric rule 2: clear permissive licences; security policies, signed releases and CVE handling for the format libraries not verified; inherits host controls. |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | Files in the customer's repository; runs anywhere, including air-gapped. |
| Ecosystem | 3 | Two vendor-originated formats plus CLI tooling, langchain-prompty and LangSmith GitHub sync; no single standard. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Git practice is mature; the formats are young (Prompty v2, Dotprompt 0.2.0) and Promptfoo is pre-1.0 and changing ownership. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Free and open source; engineering effort to build runtime delivery and trace linkage. |
| Lock-in / portability | 4 | Base 5 (plain files under customer control, permissive licences) reduced by 1 because the example eval tool's ownership is changing and the formats are not under neutral governance. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.60 / 3.65** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rubric rule 2 (self-hosted libraries and open formats): enterprise readiness and security scored on what the pattern enables and on project hygiene, each capped at 4; inherits host controls

**Capabilities.** Prompts as files in the application repository: Prompty (.prompty, markdown with YAML front matter for model, connection and template settings) or Dotprompt (executable Handlebars-based templates, language- and provider-agnostic); changes go through code review and CI, where a CLI such as Promptfoo evaluates the prompt files [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S067: Prompty README (Microsoft) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/prompty/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S066: Dotprompt README (Google) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/dotprompt/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S068: Promptfoo README (Promptfoo (OpenAI)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Uses the firm's existing change-management controls (review, approval, branch protection, release tagging) without a new vendor [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Open formats with permissive licences: Prompty MIT, Dotprompt Apache-2.0, Promptfoo MIT [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S008: prompty on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / Microsoft Prompty) <https://pypi.org/pypi/prompty/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S065: dotpromptz on PyPI (PyPI / Google) <https://pypi.org/pypi/dotpromptz/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S068: Promptfoo README (Promptfoo (OpenAI)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Multi-language runtimes: Prompty for Python, TypeScript, Rust and C#; Dotprompt for JS/TS, Python, Go, Rust and Java [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S067: Prompty README (Microsoft) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/prompty/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S066: Dotprompt README (Google) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/dotprompt/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- One artefact can carry prompt, model and parameter settings, so the release pins them together [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S067: Prompty README (Microsoft) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/prompty/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Limitations and risks**

- No runtime label switching, segmentation or instant rollback without a deployment; trace linkage must be built [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Two competing formats, both pre-1.0 or recently re-versioned (Dotprompt Python 0.2.0; Prompty v2) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S065: dotpromptz on PyPI (PyPI / Google) <https://pypi.org/pypi/dotpromptz/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S067: Prompty README (Microsoft) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/prompty/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Promptfoo: OpenAI announced its acquisition on 9 March 2026, closing date not published; Promptfoo states it is part of OpenAI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S068: Promptfoo README (Promptfoo (OpenAI)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S042: OpenAI to acquire Promptfoo (with TechCrunch via Yahoo Finance, SDxCentral, Security Boulevard) <https://openai.com/blog/openai-to-acquire-promptfoo> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Non-engineers cannot change prompts without a pull request, which is a feature for control and a cost for agility [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- Always, as the system of record for approved prompts and configuration in a regulated firm [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- As the only mechanism when business users must test prompt variants daily; pair it with a registry that CI publishes to [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C5-langsmith-prompts, C5-langfuse-prompts, C5-promptlayer

**Regulated-FS note.** Make the repository the change record that model-risk and audit teams inspect: pull-request approval by a second person, CODEOWNERS for the risk owner, eval results attached to the PR, and a signed release tag pinning prompt, model and retrieval versions [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## PromptLayer (Prompt Registry) (`C5-promptlayer`)

**Tier:** Tactical · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Strong identity controls and rollout features, but security evidence is vendor-stated, pricing is unverified and it duplicates the registry built into the L9 platforms [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Versioned registry, release labels, staged rollout, segmentation and A/B testing, evals and tracing; approval workflow not documented. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | SSO, SCIM, group-role mapping, SSO enforcement, audit log and granular RBAC verified on Enterprise; SLA not verified. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Vendor-stated SOC 2 Type 2 with a DPA committing to annual SOC 2 Type II audits and penetration tests; no ISO 27001; report not seen. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | SaaS, customer AWS account and self-hosted (Enterprise); air-gap and on-premises not verified. |
| Ecosystem | 3 | REST API, Python/JS SDKs, OTel tracing for major provider SDKs, webhooks; smaller ecosystem than the platform vendors. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Independent, continuous releases on the 1.5.x SDK line since 2022; funding not verified. |
| Cost / TCO | 2 | Pricing not publicly verified; self-hosting and identity features need an Enterprise contract. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Proprietary template API, but templates are text retrievable by API; no Git sync documented. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.40 / 3.40** | |

**Capabilities.** Prompt Registry with versioned templates; release labels (e.g. 'prod') select the served version and support staged rollouts, user segmentation and A/B testing via dynamic release labels; SDK fetches templates and can proxy provider calls for logging; evals and OpenTelemetry tracing alongside [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S004: promptlayer on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / PromptLayer) <https://pypi.org/pypi/promptlayer/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S088: PromptLayer docs: Release Labels <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagnivOrg/prompt-layer-docs/main/features/prompt-registry/release-labels.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Release labels support staged rollout and segmentation of users to prompt versions, closest to feature-flag practice among the registries [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S088: PromptLayer docs: Release Labels <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagnivOrg/prompt-layer-docs/main/features/prompt-registry/release-labels.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Enterprise Identity: SSO (SAML/OIDC via WorkOS), SCIM, group-to-role mapping, SSO enforcement, org-scoped audit log and granular RBAC [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S086: PromptLayer docs: Enterprise Identity overview <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagnivOrg/prompt-layer-docs/main/why-promptlayer/enterprise-identity/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Deployable into the customer's AWS account or self-hosted on Enterprise [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S085: PromptLayer docs: Self-Hosted PromptLayer <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagnivOrg/prompt-layer-docs/main/self-hosted.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S087: PromptLayer docs: Deploy PromptLayer on AWS <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagnivOrg/prompt-layer-docs/main/enterprise-deployments/aws.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Independent; no acquisition found [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S004: promptlayer on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / PromptLayer) <https://pypi.org/pypi/promptlayer/json> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Limitations and risks**

- SOC 2 Type 2 is a vendor statement; no report or ISO 27001 seen [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C5-S003: PromptLayer FAQ; Pricing; Data Processing Addendum 2026 <https://docs.promptlayer.com/features/faq> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Pricing and EU region not publicly verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Proprietary template API; no Git synchronisation documented [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S004: promptlayer on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / PromptLayer) <https://pypi.org/pypi/promptlayer/json> accessed 2026-10-07] [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Small vendor; funding not publicly verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- You want a standalone, model- and framework-neutral prompt registry with segmentation, and can run it in your own AWS account [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- ISO 27001 is a procurement gate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You already run Langfuse or LangSmith as the L9 platform, which would duplicate the registry [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C5-langfuse-prompts, C5-langsmith-prompts, C5-launchdarkly-ai-configs

**Regulated-FS note.** Request the SOC 2 Type II report and subprocessor list before use with client data, prefer the customer-AWS deployment, and do not use the SDK proxy mode for regulated traffic unless the gateway (C1) is bypassed by design [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## LaunchDarkly AgentControl (formerly AI Configs; API unchanged) (`C5-launchdarkly-ai-configs`)

**Tier:** Tactical · **Flags:** Renamed · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Strongest certifications and rollout mechanics in the control, but SaaS-only with unverified residency scope and proprietary configuration delivery [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Runtime configuration of model, parameters and messages, per-context targeting, defaults, metrics, online evals and approvals; prompt diffing and Git-based review not documented. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | SAML SSO, Enterprise custom roles, audit log API and Enterprise uptime SLA; SSO and roles evidence is a search extract of older pages (medium confidence); SCIM not verified. |
| Security and compliance | 4 | SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27701 and FedRAMP Moderate are company-level; AgentControl's coverage is not stated, so one below 5 (CP2 Q4). |
| Deployment flexibility | 2 | Multi-tenant SaaS, an EU-hosted offering without region detail, and a US federal instance; no self-host or VPC. |
| Ecosystem | 3 | Established feature-management platform with an Apache-2.0 AI SDK; AI-specific integrations not evidenced beyond the Python SDK. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Parent platform long-established, but the AI product is about 16 months GA and was renamed and repositioned in May 2026. |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | Transparent pricing (US$10 per service connection per month with 5,000 AI runs; US$5 per extra 1,000), but metered on every model call. |
| Lock-in / portability | 2 | Proprietary service and SDK; code-side defaults reduce runtime dependency but no export path is documented. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.30 / 3.20** | |

**Capabilities.** AgentControl (formerly AI Configs; API unchanged) delivers model name, parameters and prompt messages per user context from the LaunchDarkly feature-management service, with variable interpolation, a code-side default if the service is unavailable, and a tracker recording tokens, latency and success per configuration; online evals with custom judges GA 11 March 2026; agents, trends and approvals added [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S089: LaunchDarkly Server-Side AI SDK for Python README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/launchdarkly/python-server-sdk-ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S117: LaunchDarkly: Introducing AgentControl; AI Configs is now GA; AgentControl API docs <https://launchdarkly.com/blog/introducing-agentcontrol/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S045: AgentControl API docs (LaunchDarkly) <https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/agentcontrol> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- Feature-flag style targeting and rollout of model and prompt configuration per user context, with a code-side default as the failure mode [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S089: LaunchDarkly Server-Side AI SDK for Python README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/launchdarkly/python-server-sdk-ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27701 and FedRAMP Moderate (Federal instance); Enterprise uptime SLA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S119: LaunchDarkly Trust, security, and privacy; Platform overview; Security Program Addendum <https://launchdarkly.com/security/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S065: LaunchDarkly Trust, security, and privacy (with Security Program Addendum, docs) <https://launchdarkly.com/security/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- SAML SSO with IdP-managed roles, Enterprise custom roles and an audit log API with before-and-after versions of each change [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C5-S001: Using SSO with LaunchDarkly; Configure SAML SSO; Creating custom roles <https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/account/sso> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-C5-S002: LaunchDarkly API: Audit log (list/search/get entries) <https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/audit-log> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Published per-run pricing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S118: LaunchDarkly Pricing; subscriptions and plans; calculating billing <https://launchdarkly.com/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- Multi-tenant SaaS only; EU residency offered but regions and data scope not detailed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S119: LaunchDarkly Trust, security, and privacy; Platform overview; Security Program Addendum <https://launchdarkly.com/security/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Proprietary configuration service and SDK; no export path verified [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S089: LaunchDarkly Server-Side AI SDK for Python README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/launchdarkly/python-server-sdk-ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Renamed and repositioned twice in about a year (GA May 2025, AgentControl May 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S117: LaunchDarkly: Introducing AgentControl; AI Configs is now GA; AgentControl API docs <https://launchdarkly.com/blog/introducing-agentcontrol/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Every model call and judge run counts as a billable AI run [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S118: LaunchDarkly Pricing; subscriptions and plans; calculating billing <https://launchdarkly.com/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Choose when**

- LaunchDarkly is already the firm's feature-management standard and you need per-segment rollout and kill switches for model and prompt choices [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- Configuration must be held in the UK or EU with documented regions, or in-estate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Volume is high and per-run metering would dominate the cost [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C5-promptlayer, C5-langfuse-prompts, C5-prompts-as-code

**Regulated-FS note.** Keep the approved prompt text in Git and use AgentControl only to choose between approved, pinned variants; record the variation key on every trace, confirm EU data scope and audit-log retention on the contracted plan [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

# C6: AI FinOps

## FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS) (`C6-finops-focus`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Open, foundation-governed schema that removes tool lock-in from cost data; strategic as the data model, not as a product [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 3 | Covers cost and usage normalisation; AI model identity not yet ratified and token type deferred. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Rubric rule 2: enables a common cost dataset and chargeback inside the estate; no commercial support of its own. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Rubric rule 2: a specification with clear CC BY 4.0 licence and a validator; inherits the controls of the data platform it lands in. |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | Specification; implemented anywhere. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | FinOps Foundation, validator and vendor mappings (e.g. Vantage); AI-provider adoption not verified. |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | Ratified releases on a semi-annual cadence since 2024 under the Joint Development Foundation; AI scope still in progress. |
| Cost / TCO | 5 | Free open specification. |
| Lock-in / portability | 5 | Open standard, permissive licence, neutral governance. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.80 / 3.85** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rubric rule 2 (open specification): enterprise readiness and security scored on what the specification enables and on hygiene, each capped at 4; inherits host controls

**Capabilities.** Open specification for cost and usage data. FOCUS 1.4 was ratified on 4 June 2026; 1.2 added virtual-currency columns for credits and tokens; tokens are carried today through SKU IDs, ConsumedUnit and ConsumedQuantity. FOCUS 1.5 (no ratification date) is scoped to add AI pricing dimensions on SkuPriceDetails and four model-identity properties (ModelDeveloper, ModelFamily, ModelId, ModelVersion) with no new columns; a first-class token-type (input/output) column is deferred [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S049: FOCUS Specification CHANGELOG (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS Working Group)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FinOps-Open-Cost-and-Usage-Spec/FOCUS_Spec/working_draft/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S116: FOCUS 1.5 Release Scope; FOCUS for AI; Introducing FOCUS 1.2; Introducing FOCUS 1.4 (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS)) <https://focus.finops.org/focus-1-5-release-scope/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S046: FOCUS 1.5 Release Scope: Confirmed and Stretch Features (with Introducing FOCUS 1.4; FOCUS for AI) (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS)) <https://focus.finops.org/focus-1-5-release-scope/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- Vendor-neutral target schema for normalising gateway logs, provider invoices and cloud bills [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S048: FOCUS Specification README (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS Working Group)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FinOps-Open-Cost-and-Usage-Spec/FOCUS_Spec/working_draft/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Free, CC BY 4.0, with a conformance validator (2.2.1, August 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S096: FOCUS Specification licence (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS Working Group)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FinOps-Open-Cost-and-Usage-Spec/FOCUS_Spec/working_draft/license.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S050: focus-validator on PyPI (PyPI / FinOps Foundation) <https://pypi.org/pypi/focus-validator/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Steady cadence: six public releases since June 2023 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S049: FOCUS Specification CHANGELOG (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS Working Group)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FinOps-Open-Cost-and-Usage-Spec/FOCUS_Spec/working_draft/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07]
- FinOps Framework 2026 adds a FinOps for AI category; vendors such as Vantage map to FOCUS [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S115: FinOps Framework 2026; State of FinOps 2026; FinOps for AI technology category; Tokenomics working group; Who sets the AI budget? (FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S113: Vantage blog: Managed AI Tags; Support for Anthropic Costs; Support for Claude Enterprise Costs; OpenAI cost tools <https://www.vantage.sh/blog/managed-ai-tags> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- No AI-specific columns today; model identity arrives only with 1.5, which has no date, and token type is deferred [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S116: FOCUS 1.5 Release Scope; FOCUS for AI; Introducing FOCUS 1.2; Introducing FOCUS 1.4 (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS)) <https://focus.finops.org/focus-1-5-release-scope/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S046: FOCUS 1.5 Release Scope: Confirmed and Stretch Features (with Introducing FOCUS 1.4; FOCUS for AI) (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS)) <https://focus.finops.org/focus-1-5-release-scope/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- It is a data model only: no metering, budgets or enforcement [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Adoption by AI providers not publicly verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- Always, as the target schema for the firm's AI cost dataset [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- Do not wait for 1.5 to start: map tokens to SKU and ConsumedQuantity now [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C6-vantage, C6-cloudzero, C6-gateway-cost-attribution

**Regulated-FS note.** A FOCUS-shaped AI cost dataset makes provider spend comparable for concentration analysis and lets cost allocation feed the outsourcing register without vendor-specific mapping [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Gateway-native and provider-native token cost tracking, budgets and chargeback (pattern) (`C6-gateway-cost-attribution`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** Acquired · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* The only place where AI spend can be attributed per request and stopped in real time; implementations are replaceable behind the OpenAI-compatible interface. Acquired refers to Portkey [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Per-key/team/user/customer budgets, rate limits, spend tracking, provider and cloud reconciliation data; cost per task needs a trace join and some controls fail open by default. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | Rubric rule 2 (pattern): implementations offer SSO, RBAC and audit (LiteLLM Enterprise SSO, RBAC, SCIM and audit logs; cloud IAM under CP2 Q1); capped at 4. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Depends on implementation: LiteLLM SOC 2 Type 2 (September 2026), Cloudflare AI Gateway named in SOC 2 scope; LiteLLM's March 2026 supply-chain incident; Admin API keys are powerful credentials. |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | Self-hosted gateways, managed cloud gateways and SaaS gateways; runs in-estate or air-gapped. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | OpenAI-compatible gateway endpoints and provider admin APIs; FOCUS mapping not native. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Cloud cost tags are mature, but Foundry project attribution is preview, LiteLLM had a supply-chain incident, and Portkey changed owner. |
| Cost / TCO | 4 | Open-source core; a database is needed for budgets and spend tracking. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Base 4 (open interfaces, OSS gateways) reduced by 1 because a named implementation (Portkey) changed owner; cost data models differ per gateway. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.85 / 3.70** | |

*Evidence rules applied:* Rubric rule 2 (pattern): enterprise readiness and security scored on what implementations enable and on their hygiene, each capped at 4; platform controls presumed for cloud gateways (CP2 Q1); confirm per service

**Capabilities.** Pattern: the gateway (C1) issues virtual keys per team, project, user or customer and records tokens and cost per request, enforcing budgets and rate limits (LiteLLM: budgets at key, user, team and customer level, TPM/RPM limits); provider admin APIs (Anthropic Usage & Cost Admin API) and cloud billing tags (Bedrock application inference profiles, Microsoft Foundry project tags) are the reconciliation sources [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S010: litellm on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / BerriAI) <https://pypi.org/pypi/litellm/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S070: Usage and Cost Admin API (Claude Platform docs) (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api> accessed 2026-10-07; B-C6-S004: Amazon Bedrock user guide: Application inference profiles; Best practices for cost attribution (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-application-inference-profiles.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-C6-S005: Plan and manage costs - Microsoft Foundry <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/manage-costs> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- The gateway sees every model call, so it is the only point that can both attribute and stop spend in real time [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Mature open-source implementation with budgets, limits and spend tracking (LiteLLM MIT core) and managed equivalents in the cloud gateways (token limits and quotas in Azure APIM, Apigee and Kong; spend limits in Cloudflare) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S024: Apigee AI solutions: gateway to enterprise-ready AI (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/solutions/apigee-ai> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S016: Kong AI Gateway 2.0 Is Now GA — And It's Already Moving Faster (Kong Inc.) <https://konghq.com/blog/product-releases/kong-ai-gateway-2-0-ga> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S019: Cloudflare AI Gateway docs: Pricing, Features, Changelog; Cloudflare blog spend limits (Cloudflare, Inc.) <https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/reference/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Provider-side data breaks tokens into uncached input, cached input, cache creation and output, by API key, workspace, model and service tier, for reconciliation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S070: Usage and Cost Admin API (Claude Platform docs) (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Cloud billing tags carry AI spend into the existing cost tools (Cost Explorer and CUR; Azure cost analysis) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C6-S004: Amazon Bedrock user guide: Application inference profiles; Best practices for cost attribution (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-application-inference-profiles.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-C6-S005: Plan and manage costs - Microsoft Foundry <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/manage-costs> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- Some LiteLLM controls fail open or are off by default: max_budget without a database, and a proxy admin key that bypasses budget checks [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Cloud billing tags are aggregated per usage type per day, not per request; per-request attribution needs invocation logs or gateway data [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C6-S004: Amazon Bedrock user guide: Application inference profiles; Best practices for cost attribution (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-application-inference-profiles.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Gateway consolidation: Portkey acquired by Palo Alto Networks (completed 29 May 2026) and folded into Prisma AIRS [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S011: Palo Alto Networks Completes Acquisition of Portkey to Secure AI Agents (and 30 Apr 2026 announcement) <https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/company/press/2026/palo-alto-networks-completes-acquisition-of-portkey-to-secure-ai-agents> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S025: Palo Alto Networks Completes Acquisition of Portkey to Secure AI Agents (with PANW FY2026 10-K and 10-Q, SDxCentral) <https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/company/press/2026/palo-alto-networks-completes-acquisition-of-portkey-to-secure-ai-agents> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- LiteLLM suffered a PyPI supply-chain compromise on 24 March 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S008: Security Update: Suspected Supply Chain Incident (and Security Townhall Updates) (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-update-march-2026> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S027: LiteLLM PyPI supply chain attack (with NetSPI, Comet, Snyk/Datadog reporting) (FutureSearch) <https://futuresearch.ai/blog/litellm-pypi-supply-chain-attack/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Cost per task needs a join between gateway records and traces (L9); no product does this end to end in the fact base [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- Always, as the metering and enforcement point for model spend [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- Never as the only record: reconcile against provider invoices and cloud bills monthly [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C6-helicone, C6-vantage, C6-cloudzero

**Regulated-FS note.** Budget enforcement is an operational-resilience control against runaway agents; test that budgets fail closed, restrict the admin key, and reconcile gateway spend to invoices for the outsourcing register [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Vantage (cloud cost management platform) (`C6-vantage`)

**Tier:** Tactical · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Useful reporting layer for organisations already using it; SaaS-only with unverified residency and vendor-described AI features [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 3 | Provider integrations, AI tag normalisation and hierarchical allocation; billing-level granularity only, and features described in vendor blogs. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | SAML SSO verified (lifts NPV cap to max 3 under CP2 Q2); RBAC and audit logs not verified; SAML plan availability conflicts between pages. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 1 Type 2, reports on request; no ISO 27001 found. |
| Deployment flexibility | 2 | SaaS only; regions not verified. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | AI-provider and cloud billing integrations, API, MCP server and FOCUS-mapped schema. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Established cloud cost vendor; AI features added from 2025; ownership and funding not verified. |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | Managed AI Tags at no extra cost; AI spend counts toward quota tiers whose prices were not verified. |
| Lock-in / portability | 3 | Proprietary SaaS, but FOCUS-mapped data and an API make export feasible. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **2.95 / 2.90** | |

**Capabilities.** Cloud cost management platform that ingests cloud and AI-provider billing (Anthropic tokens by model, workspace, API key and service tier; Claude Enterprise; OpenAI tokens by model and operation), allocates it via virtual tagging and hierarchical allocation, normalises AI spend with Managed AI Tags (model, provider, token type) and exposes data through an API and an MCP server; its internal schema maps to FOCUS [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S113: Vantage blog: Managed AI Tags; Support for Anthropic Costs; Support for Claude Enterprise Costs; OpenAI cost tools <https://www.vantage.sh/blog/managed-ai-tags> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S090: Vantage MCP Server README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vantage-sh/vantage-mcp-server/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Direct AI-provider integrations, with Anthropic GA September 2025 and Claude Enterprise added July 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S113: Vantage blog: Managed AI Tags; Support for Anthropic Costs; Support for Claude Enterprise Costs; OpenAI cost tools <https://www.vantage.sh/blog/managed-ai-tags> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Managed AI Tags normalise model, provider and token type across providers at no extra cost [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S113: Vantage blog: Managed AI Tags; Support for Anthropic Costs; Support for Claude Enterprise Costs; OpenAI cost tools <https://www.vantage.sh/blog/managed-ai-tags> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 (reports on request) and self-service SAML SSO [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C6-S001: Vantage Security and Compliance; Vantage docs: Single Sign-On; SOC 1 Type 2 blog <https://www.vantage.sh/legal/security> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Schema mapped to FOCUS [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S113: Vantage blog: Managed AI Tags; Support for Anthropic Costs; Support for Claude Enterprise Costs; OpenAI cost tools <https://www.vantage.sh/blog/managed-ai-tags> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- AI cost features are described in vendor blog posts [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S113: Vantage blog: Managed AI Tags; Support for Anthropic Costs; Support for Claude Enterprise Costs; OpenAI cost tools <https://www.vantage.sh/blog/managed-ai-tags> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Anthropic integration uses an Admin API key, which has revocable read-write access [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S113: Vantage blog: Managed AI Tags; Support for Anthropic Costs; Support for Claude Enterprise Costs; OpenAI cost tools <https://www.vantage.sh/blog/managed-ai-tags> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- SaaS only; EU region, RBAC and audit logs not publicly verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Billing data is per provider account, not per task; cost per commentary still needs gateway and trace data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- Vantage is already the cloud FinOps tool and you want AI provider spend in the same allocation and showback model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You cannot accept a third party holding a read-write provider admin key [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You need per-request or per-task attribution, which belongs to the gateway [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C6-cloudzero, C6-gateway-cost-attribution, C6-finops-focus

**Regulated-FS note.** Treat it as the showback and chargeback reporting layer, fed by provider billing and gateway exports; assess the admin-key access under C4 and C7 and the platform under the outsourcing register [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Capabilities.** Cloud cost intelligence platform that ingests token-level usage and cost from OpenAI, the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock (including Claude Platform on AWS) and Azure OpenAI, and allocates it by customer, feature, team, product and environment through its CostFormation engine; a Kubernetes agent supplies container telemetry [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S114: CloudZero blog posts on AI cost (token-based pricing, Bedrock, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) <https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/token-based-pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S091: CloudZero Agent README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cloudzero/cloudzero-agent/develop/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Anthropic ingestion breaks out uncached input, cache hits, output and tool usage by model, workspace and API key (vendor statement) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S114: CloudZero blog posts on AI cost (token-based pricing, Bedrock, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) <https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/token-based-pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Allocation by customer and feature supports unit economics [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S114: CloudZero blog posts on AI cost (token-based pricing, Bedrock, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) <https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/token-based-pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 listed in the Trust Center; SAML SSO with custom roles that scope data access and map to IdP groups [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C6-S002: CloudZero Trust Center; CloudZero security page <https://trust.cloudzero.com/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-C6-S003: CloudZero docs: Users & Permissions; SSO with SAML; View and Manage Roles <https://docs.cloudzero.com/docs/users-and-permissions> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- AI cost claims are from CloudZero's own blog posts [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S114: CloudZero blog posts on AI cost (token-based pricing, Bedrock, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) <https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/token-based-pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- No ISO 27001 found; SOC reports under NDA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C6-S002: CloudZero Trust Center; CloudZero security page <https://trust.cloudzero.com/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]
- Pricing, EU region and audit logs not publicly verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Proprietary allocation engine; FOCUS support not evidenced [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- CloudZero is already the cost platform and you want AI spend allocated by customer or product next to Kubernetes costs [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- Residency of billing metadata must be documented in the UK or EU [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- You want allocation rules in an open schema [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C6-vantage, C6-gateway-cost-attribution, C6-finops-focus

**Regulated-FS note.** Use for showback where already contracted; keep the allocation rules documented outside the tool so chargeback survives an exit [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

# C7: AI security

## HashiCorp Vault (IBM Vault Self-Managed; HCP Vault Dedicated) (`C7-hashicorp-vault`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** Acquired · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Strategic for secrets and agent credential brokerage, conditional on accepting BUSL and IBM ownership (lock-in 2) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 4 | Leading depth in secrets and agent credential brokerage; not a prompt-injection or supply-chain control. |
| Enterprise readiness | 4 | Policy ACLs, namespaces (multi-tenancy), SCIM 2.0, audit devices and IBM support lifecycle; human SSO and SLA not verified in the dataset. |
| Security and compliance | 4 | SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 with IBM Vault in scope (anchor 4); no CMK/BYOK, ISO 42001 or FedRAMP evidence for 5. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | HCP Vault Dedicated plus self-managed on-prem; air-gap not verified. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | API, CLI, Terraform provider and validated IdPs (IBM Verify, Auth0, PingFederate, Entra, Okta). |
| Reliability and maturity | 4 | Years of production use and IBM lifecycle; IBM ownership change (February 2025) and 2.0 major-version transition noted. |
| Cost / TCO | 3 | BUSL community use free; Enterprise needed for agentic IAM; HCP hourly pricing published. |
| Lock-in / portability | 2 | Source-available BUSL (base 3), reduced by 1 for the 2025 acquisition (rule 3); licence risk under rule 4. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.80 / 3.65** | |

**Capabilities.** Secrets storage and brokerage, dynamic credentials and certificates, identity-based authorisation; agentic IAM (GA in Vault Enterprise 2.1, 1 September 2026) registers agents, validates IdP OAuth JWTs, enforces user, agent-ceiling and request-scoped authorisation, and records user and agent in audit logs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S034: HashiCorp Vault agentic IAM is now generally available (HashiCorp (IBM)) <https://www.hashicorp.com/en/blog/hashicorp-vault-agentic-iam-is-now-generally-available> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S061: HashiCorp Vault CHANGELOG (HashiCorp / IBM) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hashicorp/vault/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Strengths**

- Keeps credentials out of the model with short-lived, request-scoped issuance and dual attribution [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S034: HashiCorp Vault agentic IAM is now generally available (HashiCorp (IBM)) <https://www.hashicorp.com/en/blog/hashicorp-vault-agentic-iam-is-now-generally-available> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001/27017/27018 with IBM Vault in scope; FIPS 140-2 for Enterprise [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S035: HashiCorp Compliance Overview / Security at HashiCorp (HashiCorp (IBM)) <https://www.hashicorp.com/en/trust/compliance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Namespaces, SCIM 2.0, policy ACLs and audit devices [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S033: Vault release notes 2.x; IBM Vault Self-Managed 2.x.x lifecycle page (HashiCorp (IBM)) <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/updates/release-notes> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S034: HashiCorp Vault agentic IAM is now generally available (HashiCorp (IBM)) <https://www.hashicorp.com/en/blog/hashicorp-vault-agentic-iam-is-now-generally-available> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- IBM lifecycle: two years support plus extensions [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S033: Vault release notes 2.x; IBM Vault Self-Managed 2.x.x lifecycle page (HashiCorp (IBM)) <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/updates/release-notes> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

**Limitations and risks**

- BUSL 1.1 (IBM licensor) restricts competing hosted or embedded offerings [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S060: HashiCorp Vault LICENSE (BUSL 1.1) (HashiCorp / IBM) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hashicorp/vault/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Agentic IAM is Enterprise-only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S034: HashiCorp Vault agentic IAM is now generally available (HashiCorp (IBM)) <https://www.hashicorp.com/en/blog/hashicorp-vault-agentic-iam-is-now-generally-available> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Owned by IBM since 27 February 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S032: IBM Completes Acquisition of HashiCorp, Creates Comprehensive, End-to-End Hybrid Cloud Platform <https://newsroom.ibm.com/2025-02-27-ibm-completes-acquisition-of-hashicorp,-creates-comprehensive,-end-to-end-hybrid-cloud-platform> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- Version caveat: changelog stops at 2.1.1 but a v2.1.2 tag exists [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S061: Go module proxy @latest: OPA, SPIRE, agentgateway, envoyproxy/ai-gateway (Agent Router), hashicorp/vault (incl. v2 resolution error) and Vault CHANGELOG heading (Go module proxy (proxy.golang.org) / GitHub raw) <https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/@latest> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]

**Choose when**

- Multi-cloud or hybrid estate needing one broker for human, workload and agent credentials [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- A single cloud's native secrets service suffices and agent delegation is not needed [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** Cloud-native secrets managers, C4-entra-agent-id, C4-okta-auth0-ai-agents

**Regulated-FS note.** Use audit devices as the authoritative record of which agent obtained which credential on whose behalf; include IBM in concentration analysis if watsonx.governance is also chosen [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## Model and package supply-chain scanning (pattern): ModelScan, picklescan, fickling, Hugging Face Hub scanning, safetensors (`C7-model-supply-chain-scanning`)

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** Acquired · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Mandatory baseline pattern (safetensors by default plus scanning gate); ModelScan's owner was acquired [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 3 | Covers executable model formats competently; pattern-matching limits and no package or agent-artefact coverage. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Rule 2: CI libraries inherit host controls; no commercial support for the open tools (commercial successors are separate products). |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Rule 2 hygiene: security policy for ModelScan, clear licences; owner acquired and components pre-1.0. |
| Deployment flexibility | 5 | Runs anywhere, including air-gapped CI. |
| Ecosystem | 4 | Hugging Face Hub uses picklescan; commercial platforms build on the same approach. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | Mostly pre-1.0; ModelScan cadence slowed after acquisition. |
| Cost / TCO | 5 | Free open source with light operations. |
| Lock-in / portability | 4 | Permissive licences and an open format (base 5), reduced by 1 because ModelScan is vendor-owned after a 2025 acquisition (rule 3). |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.65 / 3.60** | |

**Capabilities.** Pattern: safe serialisation (safetensors) plus open-source scanners (ModelScan, picklescan, fickling) in CI and at registry promotion, complemented by Hugging Face Hub-side scanning [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S082: ModelScan README (Protect AI (Palo Alto Networks)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/protectai/modelscan/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S083: picklescan README (picklescan maintainers) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S064: fickling on PyPI (PyPI / Trail of Bits) <https://pypi.org/pypi/fickling/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S007: safetensors on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / Hugging Face) <https://pypi.org/pypi/safetensors/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S037: Hugging Face Hub Security docs (malware scanning, pickle scanning, third-party scanners Protect AI and JFrog) <https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Strengths**

- safetensors removes pickle's code-execution risk ('Pickle: Unsafe, runs arbitrary code') [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C7-S006: safetensors README (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/safetensors/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-08]
- Free, local, CI-native and air-gap friendly [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S002: modelscan on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / Protect AI) <https://pypi.org/pypi/modelscan/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S006: picklescan on PyPI (JSON API) <https://pypi.org/pypi/picklescan/json> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- ModelScan publishes a security policy with GitHub advisories [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C7-S007: modelscan Security Policy (Protect AI (Palo Alto Networks)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/protectai/modelscan/main/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08]

**Limitations and risks**

- picklescan only pattern-matches module names; scanning reduces but does not remove risk [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S037: Hugging Face Hub Security docs (malware scanning, pickle scanning, third-party scanners Protect AI and JFrog) <https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- ModelScan's owner Protect AI is now Palo Alto Networks; README directs users to Guardian; last release February 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S014: Palo Alto Networks Completes Acquisition of Protect AI <https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/company/press/2025/palo-alto-networks-completes-acquisition-of-protect-ai> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S082: ModelScan README (Protect AI (Palo Alto Networks)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/protectai/modelscan/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S002: modelscan on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / Protect AI) <https://pypi.org/pypi/modelscan/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Most components pre-1.0 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S002: modelscan on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / Protect AI) <https://pypi.org/pypi/modelscan/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S064: fickling on PyPI (PyPI / Trail of Bits) <https://pypi.org/pypi/fickling/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S007: safetensors on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / Hugging Face) <https://pypi.org/pypi/safetensors/json> accessed 2026-10-07]
- Does not address package compromise (LiteLLM case) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S008: Security Update: Suspected Supply Chain Incident (and Security Townhall Updates) (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-update-march-2026> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Choose when**

- Always, as the minimum gate for self-hosted weights [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- Never as the only supply-chain control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C7-prisma-airs, C7-hiddenlayer, C7-openssf-model-signing

**Regulated-FS note.** Record scan results and artefact hashes in the model inventory (C8) so validation evidence refers to the exact weights scanned [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

## OpenSSF Model Signing (OMS) specification and model-signing library (`C7-openssf-model-signing`)

**Tier:** Tactical · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic

*Rationale:* Right standard for internally produced weights, but narrow and with unverified adoption [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Criterion | Score | Rationale |
|--------|--:|------------------------------|
| Technical | 3 | Does integrity and signer verification well; narrow scope by design. |
| Enterprise readiness | 3 | Rule 2: library inherits host controls; PKCS#11 and private Sigstore enable enterprise key custody. |
| Security and compliance | 3 | Rule 2 hygiene: foundation-governed, Apache-2.0; no security policy file found. |
| Deployment flexibility | 4 | Self-hosted library; offline key or certificate signing possible; private Sigstore supported. |
| Ecosystem | 2 | Adoption by hubs and registries not publicly verified. |
| Reliability and maturity | 3 | v1.0 spec (April 2025), library 1.1.1; no release in the last twelve months found. |
| Cost / TCO | 5 | Free. |
| Lock-in / portability | 5 | Open specification, Apache-2.0, neutral governance. |
| **Total (generic / FS)** | **3.35 / 3.50** | |

**Capabilities.** Open specification and Apache-2.0 library to sign and verify ML models of any format with a detached Sigstore bundle (DSSE/in-toto), using Sigstore, key pairs, certificates or PKCS#11 devices, with optional private Sigstore instances and a transparency log [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S040: Launch of Model Signing v1.0: OpenSSF AI/ML Working Group Secures the Machine Learning Supply Chain (OpenSSF (Linux Foundation)) <https://openssf.org/blog/2025/04/04/launch-of-model-signing-v1-0-openssf-ai-ml-working-group-secures-the-machine-learning-supply-chain/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S038: model-signing on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / Sigstore model-transparency (OpenSSF)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/model-signing/json> accessed 2026-10-07; B-C7-S005: Model Transparency README (model-signing) (Sigstore / OpenSSF) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigstore/model-transparency/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-08].

**Strengths**

- Vendor-neutral integrity and signer verification under OpenSSF (Linux Foundation) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S040: Launch of Model Signing v1.0: OpenSSF AI/ML Working Group Secures the Machine Learning Supply Chain (OpenSSF (Linux Foundation)) <https://openssf.org/blog/2025/04/04/launch-of-model-signing-v1-0-openssf-ai-ml-working-group-secures-the-machine-learning-supply-chain/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
- HSM (PKCS#11) and private Sigstore support suit regulated key custody [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C7-S005: Model Transparency README (model-signing) (Sigstore / OpenSSF) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigstore/model-transparency/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-08]
- Free [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S038: model-signing on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / Sigstore model-transparency (OpenSSF)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/model-signing/json> accessed 2026-10-07]

**Limitations and risks**

- Proves integrity and signer, not provenance or safety [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Hub and registry adoption not publicly verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- No library release on PyPI since 1.1.1 (10 October 2025) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S038: model-signing on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / Sigstore model-transparency (OpenSSF)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/model-signing/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; no security policy file found

**Choose when**

- You fine-tune or distil models internally and must prove served weights equal validated weights [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Avoid when**

- You only consume hosted model APIs [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}

**Nearest competitors:** C7-model-supply-chain-scanning, C7-hiddenlayer

**Regulated-FS note.** Sign with a firm-controlled key or HSM and verify the signature at model-server start-up [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Tier:** Strategic · **Flags:** none · **Original graphic label:** not in graphic
